544439|2026-06.headline: Crizac Q1 FY27 revenue fell 4% YoY to INR2,012 million on adverse university mix; management now guides FY27 flat versus FY26.
544439|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations was INR2,012 million, down 4% YoY and below the INR3,917 million of Q4 FY26, consistent with Q1 being the seasonal trough. Management attributed the decline to a less favourable university mix (fewer high-fee top-ranked university bonuses and slabs), not lower platform activity, as enrolments rose 15% YoY. EBITDA fell 7.6% YoY to INR600 million, with margin at 29.8% versus 31%, while PAT grew 2.9% to INR471 million. Management moved from earlier growth expectations to a flat FY27 outlook, citing flight disruption and rupee volatility expected to hit Q2, with pent-up demand expected in Q3 and Q4. It also announced a leadership change: Chairman Christopher Nagle stepped down as UK CEO and became Non-Executive Chairman of the Indian holding company, with Eric Wijmenga taking UK and Europe operations.

qa_highlights.question: Why did revenue fall QoQ and what is the Q2 outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Constant-currency revenue fell about 4% as volume rose 15% but university mix shifted; Q2 expected weaker due to Feb-June flight cancellations and rupee volatility.

qa_highlights.question: Will FY27 growth be 20-25% or 15-17% as earlier hinted?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Management now expects FY27 flat versus FY26, with pent-up demand in Q3 and Q4 offsetting Q1 and Q2 shortfalls.

qa_highlights.question: Why is standalone PBT above consolidated PBT in Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Crizac India standalone recognised some payments as revenue; investments in Crizac UK and subsidiaries should pay off in Q3.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a buyback plan given the stock trades around 11x EBITDA?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the company has only about 20% public float and SEBI rules do not allow a buyback at this level; the compliance team will look at the suggestion.

qa_highlights.question: Will the UK concentration fall, and what is the target?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, the target is to get UK share below 60% within about three years, aided by Innova (Netherlands) and other markets, though policy shifts will slow this.

qa_highlights.question: Will value-added services become material?
qa_highlights.answer: Not initially; they could add 2-5% to EBITDA and 1-1.5% of revenue over the next couple of years, with ForeignAdmits accelerating this.

qa_highlights.question: Is the dividend a one-time payout?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Management said the DRHP commits to a minimum 40% of PAT as dividend for at least three years; FY26 is done, leaving at least two more years.

544441|2026-03.headline: Meta Infotech FY26 revenue rose 23% to INR270 crore but PAT fell to INR11 crore; management targets 4x PAT by FY29 with no numeric guidance.
544441|2026-03.overview: FY26 was described as an investment year: revenue grew 23% YoY to INR270 crore and H2 revenue grew 72% YoY to INR60 crore, but EBITDA fell to INR18 crore (FY25: INR25 crore) and PAT fell to INR11 crore (FY25: INR14 crore). Management attributed the squeeze to new hires, geographic expansion, 12 new vendor onboardings, a Thales-owned Imperva transition that cut professional services revenue from about INR8.5 crore to INR2 crore, and a forex loss on a large contract. The company set an aspirational target of up to 4x PAT by FY29 from FY26 levels, without numeric revenue or margin guidance. Order book stood at INR506 crore as of May 2026, about 1.9x FY26 revenue.

segments.commentary: Product business, including the large low-margin deal, carried H2 product EBIT loss versus about 8.2% product EBIT margin in H1 per an analyst's reading; management said it will decline product deals below 5-6% margin and target 9-10% going forward.

qa_highlights.question: What caused the drop in Imperva services revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Imperva was acquired by Thales; the existing team left, cutting Meta's professional services revenue from about INR8.5 crore in FY25 to INR2 crore in FY26, versus an expected INR10 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Why was H2 product EBIT negative and what is the margin path?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it would check the H2 segment numbers; it stated a policy to avoid product deals below 5-6% margin and to target 9-10% product margins.

qa_highlights.answer: CFO Paresh Soni said it is timing: about INR20 crore of inventory at March, expected to sell in April; tax payments also weighed on operating cash flow.

qa_highlights.question: Does the company need more equity or debt?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no extra funding is needed for growth; the IPO was not required for expansion, and it cited delayed billing from forex-linked contracts.

544443|2026-03.headline: Travel Food Services Q4 system-wide sales grew 27.7% YoY to INR9 billion, while FY26 adjusted consolidated PAT rose 21.5% to INR4.5 billion on about 1% traffic growth.
544443|2026-03.overview: Management described FY26 as a disruption-heavy year (India-Pakistan conflict, aircraft crash-related schedule cuts, FDTL crew rest curbs, Middle East conflict from March 2026) in which TFS airport passenger traffic grew only 1.2%. Despite this, system-wide sales grew 25.4% to INR32.1 billion, driven by 9.4% like-for-like growth and 13.1% net contract gains. Q4 saw gross margin of 87.3% (85.6% after a one-time reclassification) and EBITDA up 38.3%, but PAT growth was held to about 15% by a INR212 million litigation provision and a weaker JV contribution. Trade receivables rose to about INR2.64 billion at year-end on EATS ramp-up, which management expects to normalise by H1 FY27.

segments.commentary: About 55% of FY26 consolidated revenue; growth driven by throughput, menu engineering and value combos.

segments.name: Lounges
segments.commentary: About 41% of FY26 consolidated revenue; growth from premiumisation and dwell time. Kyra Lounge opened at Hong Kong International Airport and a Cochin lounge opened in the year.

segments.name: Management and other services
segments.commentary: About 4% of FY26 consolidated revenue.

guidance_outlook: Gross margin expected in the 80% to 83% range for FY27 overall, with some inflationary pressure from LPG prices linked to the Middle East conflict.
Capex averaging INR50 crore to INR60 crore a year, including FY27, mainly for unit mobilisation at Delhi, Cochin and upcoming Noida.
Receivables (about INR264 crore at year-end vs INR100-110 crore average) expected to normalise to 40-45 days by H1 FY27.
Management expects FY27 passenger traffic growth of around 5%, per public reports, with Q1 FY27 still affected by the war-like situation.
Annual dividend of INR10.25 per share for FY26, subject to shareholder approval.
Bhogapuram (Vizag) contract under GHL expected to add about seven outlets; Noida airport operations expected to start in the coming months.
capex_capacity: Pipeline of more than 50 outlets, all committed per management.
Network now covers 20 airports and more than 550 travel QSR outlets and lounges; 76 travel QSR units mobilised in FY26 (including Delhi, Mumbai, Ahmedabad, Cochin, Navi Mumbai).
Noida airport on track to start operations in the coming months; two more airports in the works in the coming months.
International: Malaysia lounges expanded to three airports; second Hong Kong lounge opened in Q4; subsidiaries in Dubai and Indonesia.
Delhi T3 concession expired in February 2026; a six-month short-term extension was granted, and the company plans to bid through its JV GHL when it comes up.
demand_pricing: Passenger traffic at TFS airports grew 1.2% in FY26; Q4 was broadly flat YoY, with January up, February flat and March/April weaker on international traffic.
Management said domestic traffic was robust while international traffic fell nearly double digits in March-April, especially at southern airports and Goa.
Food inflation was about 3% to 5% in April per management; price hikes taken in line with inflation; key supplier contracts are annual.
Management said the mass-market credit card lounge access curbs are offset by premium cards growing more than 50%, with premium cardholders being frequent flyers.
Management expects LFL to be driven by about 7% to 10% passenger traffic plus about 7% to 10% from price and initiatives (combined).

qa_highlights.question: How is Q1 FY27 trading, given last year's Q1 was hit by India-Pakistan conflict?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said January was strong, February was muted, March and April were weak on international traffic, and early May shows improving trends versus March and April.

qa_highlights.question: Inorganic growth in FY27 and risk from Kolkata airport privatisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not guide numbers; cited 11 airports in the privatisation pipeline and said Kolkata's inclusion or state changes are not expected to alter the schedule.

qa_highlights.question: Can airport F&B pricing and energy costs be passed on?
qa_highlights.answer: Electric equipment is a large part of the cost base, giving a natural hedge; food inflation has been manageable, and price hikes follow inflation.

qa_highlights.question: Are airport concession fees rising and what is long-term economics?
qa_highlights.answer: Rentals are a normal portfolio negotiation with some going up and some down; management said nothing dramatically different is happening.

qa_highlights.question: What is the structural versus temporary Q4 EBITDA margin improvement?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the one-off reclassification of INR78 million cost reduced gross margin to 85.6% in Q4; full-year gross margin excluding it is about 84%.

qa_highlights.question: Why did finance cost rise, and what drove the receivables increase?
qa_highlights.answer: Finance cost rose due to a INR212 million litigation provision booked in full; receivables rose on EATS bank billing ramp-up and should normalise by H1 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is the steady-state LFL breakup?
qa_highlights.answer: LFL is roughly passenger traffic (7% to 10% historically) plus 7% to 10% from price and initiatives, averaged over a year.

qa_highlights.question: Capital allocation and interest in duty-free or retail?
qa_highlights.answer: Management stressed cash discipline, zero debt and ROCE of about 45%, and prioritised international lounges and expressway wayside amenities; no duty-free plans were mentioned.

EBITDA rose 11% to INR1.6 billion, but margin moderated to 35.8% on pre-operating and employee costs for new airports (Noida, Cochin, Delhi). PAT was helped by a INR131 million one-time GST provision write-back in other income.

About 90 units commissioned over last 12 months expected to normalise over next 12 months; benefits to play out in H2 FY27.
Over 50 outlets under development, mostly to open in FY27; 12-18 months to mature at existing terminals, 18-24 months at greenfield airports.
Pre-operating costs for Cochin, Delhi and Noida ramp-up expected to normalise in about 12 months, returning to traditional cost levels.

Bhogapuram Airport opened 17 August 2026 with multiple outlets under JV GHL.
capex_capacity: Over 50 outlets under construction or about to start construction across airports including Delhi, Navi Mumbai, Bhogapuram and Noida.
Noida International Airport outlets and passenger services commissioned in the quarter.
Asia focus for international expansion; Dubai entity set up for the Middle East and Indonesia entity set up recently to enable local bids.
Highways wayside amenities (WSA) under evaluation, with government plan of about 1,000 wayside amenities; management says medium-to-long term.

LFL growth normally runs 5-7 percentage points above passenger traffic; management did not take significant price increases this year, with growth from premiumisation, bundles and brand changes.
Mumbai and Guwahati hit by traffic migration to new airport infrastructure; South India markets hit by Middle East exposure.
Contract renewal rate moved from about 94% to 92%, attributed to non-renewal of small highway outlets.
Management says bidding discipline stays on cash return; net contract gains are lumpy and not guided.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the 4.2% LFL came from higher spend per passenger, and what is sustainable LFL?

qa_highlights.question: Lounge aggregation cost and other expenses rise in the quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: INR223 million of lounge aggregation cost sits in other expenses; excluding it, other expenses rose 22% YoY. Management expects normalisation within about 12 months.

qa_highlights.question: Why are JV and associate revenues growing slower than consolidated?
qa_highlights.answer: Some JV contracts are moving to JV structures over time, and Western airports with Middle East exposure, which form a bulk of JV portfolio, were hit.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Delhi T3 contract moving to JV in H2?

qa_highlights.question: Are the 50 outlets under development in existing airports?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, a blend of already-announced airports such as Delhi, Navi Mumbai and Bhogapuram; these were won 3-8 months ago and are in build-out.

qa_highlights.question: Highways strategy: is it accelerating?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said highways are a medium-to-long-term opportunity tied to government wayside amenity plans, with a return threshold that must be met; it will be calibrated, not immediate.

risks_watch: International traffic recovery depends on airline route restorations from September-October 2026; Middle East conflict renewed in June.
EBITDA margin (35.8%) under pressure from pre-operating and employee costs at new airports; watch normalisation in next 12 months.
Delhi T3 contract ends 30 September 2026 and the GHL JV bid outcome is unknown; it moves out of consolidation.
Chennai and Kolkata renewals due end-March 2027 and early Q1 FY28 may bring cost resets.
PAT growth flattered by INR131 million one-time GST write-back; underlying growth is lower.
544443|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on medium-term growth and balance sheet, but cautious on near-term traffic; management repeatedly attributes weakness to temporary external factors. Evasive on specific numbers such as net contract gain targets and JV economics, and on the Delhi T3 bid outcome.
key_quotes: Despite the disruptions arising from the ongoing conflict in the Middle East, we delivered double -digit growth in both sales and profitability, continued to expand our network, and further strengthened our position across key airport markets.
So, in a sense, if you see, we tend to be in that range of more than passenger traffic, somewhere in the 5% to 7% above that at least in terms of performance.

In the new SPV, our shareholding with GMR is 30% and therefore it doesn't get consolidated going forward.

544444|2026-03.headline: Glen Industries H2 FY26 PAT of INR8.20 crore on INR108.60 crore income; management targets INR500 crore turnover and INR90 crore EBITDA in FY28.
544444|2026-03.overview: FY26 total income was INR205.16 crore, EBITDA INR38.50 crore and PAT INR16.50 crore, with H2 FY26 income of INR108.60 crore, EBITDA INR18.69 crore and PAT INR8.20 crore. Management attributed margin compression from about 23-24% in FY25 to about 18-19% in FY26 to passing on PLA price benefits to customers. A capacity expansion (plastic food containers roughly 3x, plus about 750 MT paper-based food packaging including paper cups) has a revised project cost of INR130-135 crore, now expected to start commercial production from September 2026. Raw material prices rose sharply after the West Asia conflict, with polypropylene peaking near INR150/kg and now about INR135/kg.

financial_highlights.metric: EBITDA margin FY26 (as cited on call)
financial_highlights.change: down from about 23-24% in FY25 per management and analyst

financial_highlights.value: Thin-wall food containers 82.72%; PLA and paper straws 17.16%; mould designing 0.12%

segments.name: Thin-wall food containers
segments.commentary: About 82.72% of FY26 revenue with capacity utilisation of about 77.74%. Raw-material price pass-through is monthly, impacting turnover by about INR2.5 crore per month during the recent price rise.

segments.name: PLA and paper straws
segments.commentary: About 17.16% of FY26 revenue; utilisation about 28.33% (PLA) and 34.13% (paper). Management says these are seasonal, peak-season-only (4-4.5 months), and sees utilisation capped near 35%; no further straw capex planned.

segments.name: Mould designing services
segments.commentary: About 0.12% of FY26 revenue.

guidance_outlook: FY28 target: turnover above INR500 crore with EBITDA of about INR90 crore (about 18-19% margin), based on pre-war raw material prices.
Expansion revenue: existing capacity about INR200-215 crore; new project adds about INR300 crore; combined about INR500 crore per annum.
FY27 incremental revenue from new capacity estimated at INR100-125 crore, depending on stabilisation speed; some revenue expected in FY27.
Commercial production targeted from September 2026, with full project operational by October-December 2026.
Management says EBITDA margin sustainable at 18-19% over the long run; paper cup margin around 18%.
Eight additional injection moulding machines (20 to 29) expected to add about INR15 crore annual revenue.
capex_capacity: Expansion project cost revised to INR130-135 crore from about INR100 crore, citing rupee depreciation (85-86 to about 96 per USD-equivalent as stated), wider scope in building and machinery, and printing machines.
Funding: INR50 crore term loan and INR50 crore IPO proceeds for original INR100 crore; incremental INR30-32 crore from internal accruals; no additional debt or equity planned.
Commissioning delayed about three months due to SIR and West Bengal elections holding up building plan approvals; commercial production now expected from September 2026.
Injection moulding machines raised from 20 to 29.
Existing land parcel remains mortgaged to bank; to be released after new facility is capitalised.
Management says no further straw capex; straw capacity sufficient for demand.
demand_pricing: PLA price about INR205/kg now vs INR195-197/kg pre-war; polypropylene about INR135/kg now vs INR90-92/kg pre-war, peaking near INR150/kg; paper stable (locally sourced).
Pass-through: PLA price changes passed on to customers from March; food container prices adjusted monthly; management says absolute margin preserved though percentage margin falls.

Raw material sourcing: about 85% imported (mainly Middle East earlier), 15% from Indian Oil; imported material from China at 5-6% price advantage; Middle East supply expected to normalise in 1-2 months.
Raw material inventory above 3 months currently; finished goods 2-2.5 months.

Customer concentration: no customer above 5-6% of total sales; top 4-5 export customers (US, UK, Greece) account for about 50-60% of export sales; over 300 domestic distributors; Parle about 25% of corporate sales as stated.
Exports: about 40 recurring international clients across Europe, US, Australia, South Korea; export revenue declined in FY26 due to lower polymer prices vs FY25, not volume or war.
Geography: eastern India about 35% of revenue; north and west next.
Competition: few national/export players in India with HACCP and FSSC certifications; management cites brand and standards as barriers.

qa_highlights.question: Why did EBITDA margin decline and what is the sustainable range?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said PLA price benefits were passed to customers in FY26, lowering margin from about 23% (FY25) to about 18-19%; sustainable range stated as 18-19%.

qa_highlights.question: Expansion capex, timeline and revenue potential?
qa_highlights.answer: Project cost revised to INR130-135 crore; commercial production from September 2026, full operations by December 2026; combined revenue potential about INR500 crore per annum.

qa_highlights.question: Utilisation of straws and paper products given seasonality?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said straw utilisation can not exceed about 35% due to 4-4.5 month peak season; paper cups are not currently manufactured, and the expansion includes paper cups with about 18% margin.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of raw material price rise on FY27 turnover?
qa_highlights.answer: Management estimated about INR2-2.5 crore per month turnover uplift from price pass-through, with no change to absolute margin; guidance remains based on pre-war prices.

qa_highlights.question: Was there any production disruption from the war?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there was no disruption; about two months of inventory was held and two months' requirement was imported from China.

risks_watch: Raw material volatility: PP and PLA prices remain elevated; management says guidance excludes current prices and could reverse within about two months of conflict ending.
Margin percentage compression in price-rising periods; EBITDA margin moved from about 17-18% to higher levels in prior halves.
Execution risk on the new project: approvals delayed about three months, commissioning expected September 2026, with capacity ramp-up pace determining FY27 revenue.
Seasonal demand in straws (beverage sector) keeping utilisation low around 28-34%.
Working capital build: raw material inventory above 3 months and inventory cycle of 5-5.5 months against about 4 months normal, affecting ROCE.
Customer and export concentration: top export accounts about 50-60% of export sales.
Undisclosed land parcel and future diversification plans; management declined to specify new products.

544447|2026-06.headline: Smartworks Q1 FY27 revenue rose 44% YoY to INR 546 crores, with normalized EBITDA margin at 19.6% and guidance of 28-30% revenue growth reaffirmed.
544447|2026-06.overview: Revenue reached INR 546 crores, up 44% YoY and 5% QoQ, while normalized EBITDA grew 74% YoY to INR 107 crores at a 19.6% margin. Normalized PAT nearly tripled YoY to INR 39 crores. Growth was supported by mature-centre occupancy (committed 92%) and a higher share of 1,000+ seat clients, GCCs and multi-city clients, though overall occupancy dipped to 81% from 82% QoQ as new centres filled up. Management reaffirmed FY27 guidance (28-30% revenue growth, 19-20% normalized EBITDA margin, 13 million sq ft by March 2027) and started a heavy capex cycle of INR 550-600 crores for the year.

financial_highlights.change: vs 16.2% in Q1 FY26 and 19% in Q4 FY26
vs negative INR 4.9 crores a year ago
vs INR 22 crores in same quarter last year

segments.name: Core rental (enterprise annuity)
segments.commentary: Enterprise annuity demand is 92% of rental revenue; 1,000+ seat cohort is 41% of revenue (37% in FY26). Committed contracted revenue is about INR 5,400 crores, covering 87% of FY27 revenue.

segments.name: GCC clients
segments.commentary: GCCs contribute 21% of revenue, up from 15% in FY26. Recent wins include a Swiss bank and a manufacturing GCC; a Japanese NBFC subsidiary took space in Mumbai.

segments.name: Singapore
segments.commentary: Work Studio acquired, taking the portfolio to over 1,500 seats (about 2% of revenue); 400-450 seats now available to sell, funded from Singapore cash flows. Management says no further meaningful expansion planned.

segments.name: Value-added services (VAS)
segments.commentary: Non-lease rental revenue rose to over INR 68 crores from INR 22 crores YoY, and is take-rate based with no direct cost. VAS guidance is not built into the FY27 projections.

guidance_outlook: Reaffirmed FY27 revenue growth of 28-30%, normalized EBITDA margin of 19-20%, and operational footprint above 13 million sq ft by March 2027.
Plans to add 2.5-3 million sq ft of operational space in FY27; more than 3.5 million sq ft signed, giving a buffer of about 0.7-0.8 million sq ft.
Capex guided at INR 550-600 crores for FY27, with heavy spend in the next two quarters.
Management expects ROCE to expand meaningfully through FY28 as capex cohorts mature.
Revenue jump expected mainly in Q3 or Q4 as new centres ramp up (about 12 months to ramp).
capex_capacity: Operational footprint 10.4 million sq ft as of June 2026; 1.9 million sq ft under fit-out; 0.3 million sq ft added in Q1 and 2.1 million sq ft over the last 12 months.

About 3 million sq ft to come online over the next 9 months, including Eastbridge (Mumbai) and Eastside (Pune), both landing in H2 FY27. Vikhroli asset is 8.15 lakh sq ft, described as the world's largest standalone managed campus.
New fit-out capex is INR 1,350 per sq ft, rising about 5% a year; refurbishment is about 15% of initial capex every three years (around INR 5 per sq ft per year, by management's estimate).
Every building needed for the next two years is secured; FY29 work has begun. Long-term rights give 10-15 years of access.
Security deposits of INR 33 crores paid to landlords to lock buildings for FY28 and part of FY29.
demand_pricing: Occupancy 81% (vs 82% in Q4 FY26), reflecting new centres still filling. Mature centres at 89% on 9.1 million sq ft; committed occupancy 92%. Management guides 80-85% occupancy over the next three quarters.

Seat retention 74% in Q1, with client count down while occupied seats and revenue rose. Management says the churn is deliberate repricing of older, lower-rate clients; the annual retention range it cited was 80-88%.
Realization on incremental mature-footprint seats leased in Q1 FY27 was about INR 181 per sq ft per month, up from about INR 170 a year earlier. Management cited a rental INR 185 per seat figure.
Mix: IT/ITES down to 35% of clients (from over 40%); target 25-30/35%. Multi-city clients 35% of revenue (31% in FY26).
Pre-commitment: about 30-35% of new buildings is pre-committed by existing or incoming clients. Landlord mix is about 65% non-institutional and 35% institutional.

qa_highlights.question: Rationale for the Singapore Work Studio acquisition, expected revenue and occupancy, and whether fit-out costs of INR 1,350 face inflation.
qa_highlights.answer: Acquired from internal cash flows at roughly construction cost; the target was about 60% occupied. Singapore is about 80,000 sq ft in total and 2% of revenue, with 400-450 seats now available to sell. Expansion will not be meaningful, and capex is set at INR 550-600 crores for FY27.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the expansion is speculative, and how much is pre-leased?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 30-35% of any new building is pre-committed by existing clients, and occupancy ramps to 80-85% within 13-14 months, as seen on prior centres.

qa_highlights.question: Is the drop in retention a sign of demand weakness, and will similar churn continue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 74% was Q2-seasonal churn; mature committed occupancy is 92%, and most churned space is already re-let. Churn is expected to fall in Q3 and Q4, as in prior years.

qa_highlights.question: Is there supply risk from developer delays?
qa_highlights.answer: Supply is covered by a buffer of 0.7-0.8 million sq ft over the 2.5-3 million sq ft target, and management is working with institutional developers such as DLF, Hiranandani, Tata, Panchshil and Salarpuria.

qa_highlights.question: How is the 28-30% guidance built, given the existing base is at 92% committed occupancy?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the base is almost fully sold, so growth depends on new centres that take about 12 months to ramp. Growth is expected to show mainly in Q3 or Q4, and the range is one management is confident about.

qa_highlights.question: Why did OCF/EBITDA dip, and what about VAS margins and pricing power?
qa_highlights.answer: The dip reflects INR 33 crores of security deposits paid to landlords. VAS is take-rate based with no direct cost, so it is margin accretive, but it is only in pilot stages and not in FY27 projections. Management said the nearest competitor prices 10-15% higher than Smartworks.

risks_watch: Occupancy may stay at 80-85% in the next three quarters as large new centres ramp, and it could drop further.
Revenue guidance depends on new-centre ramp-up and handover timing, with most of the uplift in Q3-Q4 FY27.
Capex of INR 550-600 crores is front-loaded; FCF is negative (INR -56 crores in Q1) and depends on OCF recovering after deposit payments.
IT/ITES share is falling, and management could not give a call-centre (AI-exposed) breakdown.

Revenue and EBITDA margin depend on keeping the 19-20% range while absorbing new cohorts.
Management corrected several numbers during the call (Singapore occupancy, seat count, IT/ITES share, retention), so the transcript figures should be checked against the presentation.

rows.why: Free cash flow was negative INR 56 crore in Q1 with capex of ~INR 150 crore and OCF of INR 95 crore after INR 33 crore of security deposits; net debt is INR 5.6 crore at under 9% borrowing cost, so funding pressure is modest but rising.

rows.why: Realization on incremental mature-footprint seats was about INR 181 per sq ft per month vs about INR 170 a year earlier (+6%), and the nearest competitor prices 10-15% higher, supporting pricing power.

544449|2026-03.headline: Anthem FY26 consolidated revenue Rs 2,124 crore (+18% incl. other income), with Q4 record revenue Rs 611 crore (+26% YoY) and Q4 EBITDA margin 48.1%.

Management said destocking by customers is largely behind it and refused to give FY27 or FY28 guidance. Capex is shifting to Unit 4, with Phase 1 of about Rs 1,200 crore to finish by March 2028.

segments.commentary: FY26 revenue Rs 352 crore (17%); Q4 Rs 98 crore, +8% YoY, the first revenue growth after flat first three quarters. Management aspires to around 20% growth; products include serratiopeptidase, vitamins, probiotics and enzymes, sold mainly to India and RoW markets.

Asset quality improved sequentially (GNPA 2.08%, NNPA 0.93%), but credit cost rose to INR3.69 crore (0.95%) from 0.58%, attributed mainly to vehicle finance and an extra 10% provisioning on up-money cases. Management kept FY27 PAT growth guidance of 40-45% and AUM growth of 30-35% unchanged.

544466|2026-03.headline: Aditya Infotech Q4 FY26 revenue rose 45.5% YoY to INR1,422 crore with EBITDA margin of 18%; FY27 revenue guidance raised to INR6,000-6,500 crore.

Management raised FY27 guidance to revenue INR6,000-6,500 crore, EBITDA margin 14-15% and PAT margin 8.5-9.5%. Management flagged that low-cost inventory is now exhausted and component costs (chips, memory, USD, freight) will keep rising through 2027, so price increases are being passed on monthly in small steps.

HD analog job work planned to move to EMS partners at about 0.5 million units per month. Evaluating further land in North India.

Market unit growth expected at 15-16% for FY27. Management says the industry's pent-up demand from the STQC transition was muted in FY26, and ASP increases are heavier on entry-level IP and NVR than on enterprise/project segments.
Consumer purchases are under 10% of the business; the business is largely B2B. Government is 15-20% of revenue and management plans for a similar share.

Volume vs value in FY26: volume growth about 18-20%, with the rest from ASP and mix.

qa_highlights.answer: Anup Nair cited a mix of low-cost inventory, the Q4 price rise and higher-end SKUs (STQC-certified project SKUs from H2). He said the low-cost inventory is now mostly used up, but FY27 guidance is above FY26 and slightly below Q4 margin.

qa_highlights.question: Cash conversion cycle and working capital needs with advance chip and memory purchases?
qa_highlights.answer: Anup Nair said the cash conversion cycle has risen because creditors fell as the company secured supply, and some inventory is being blocked with advance payments. Working capital is factored into FY27 plans; capex is to be funded mainly from internal accruals and some debt.

qa_highlights.question: Capex plans for FY27-28?
qa_highlights.answer: Aditya Khemka said the earlier plan of about INR200 crore has been raised to INR200-300 crore for FY27, with FY28 plans still under work. Funding is through internal accruals and some debt; the debt-equity ratio is very low.

qa_highlights.question: Export plans?
qa_highlights.answer: Aditya Khemka said export action may start in FY27, but domestic demand comes first. Some thoughts are underway and the outcome is not yet clear.

qa_highlights.question: Revenue split FY26: volume vs price?
qa_highlights.answer: Anup Nair said volume growth was about 18-20% and the rest came from ASP and mix. The price rise was mainly in Q4. For FY27, ASP growth is about 25% and volume growth 25-30%.

544477|2026-03.headline: FY26 consolidated total income rose 25.6% to INR 633.4 crore and PAT 42.0% to INR 31.8 crore, with a record INR 1,143 crore order book.
544477|2026-03.overview: Management reported FY26 consolidated total income of INR 633.4 crore (up 25.6% YoY), EBITDA of INR 51.5 crore (up 28.4%) and PAT of INR 31.8 crore (up 42.0%), with debt-to-equity at 0.45x and ROE at 18.4%. The closing order book was a record INR 1,143 crore, and the company won the Kaza Fee Plaza toll contract (about INR 328.8 crore), the largest in its history. Management said it walked away from two toll projects (Venkatapalam penalty of INR 26.33 lakh; Katiyara handed over) on commercial grounds. Most of the call focused on the wayside amenities and ropeway opportunities, and on FY27 revenue guidance of INR 950 crore.

segments.name: Tollway collection
segments.commentary: Contributed 73.7% of FY26 revenue; Kaza Fee Plaza (Andhra Pradesh, about INR 328.8 crore) is the largest toll contract won. Stated segment margin is about 7%. Toll order book balance was INR 526.1 crore as of March 2026.

segments.name: EPC infrastructure
segments.commentary: Contributed 19.8% of FY26 revenue; 105+ completed and 30+ ongoing projects. Balance EPC works INR 591.3 crore as of March 2026; stated margin 13-14% with a floor of about 13-14% GP. Order book is currently dominated by Madhya Pradesh.

segments.name: Real Estate
segments.commentary: Contributed 6.5% of FY26 revenue; revenue rose to INR 41.6 crore from INR 8.0 crore in FY25. Management cited margins of about 50%.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue guidance of about INR 950 crore: EPC about INR 300 crore and Toll about INR 650 crore (stated in Q&A).

Wayside amenities break-even estimated at 5-8 years on a 30-year contract and 3-5 (maybe 7) years on a 20-year contract; cash outlay not quantified.

Government allocated INR 3.1 lakh crore to MoRTH for FY27.
capex_capacity: Wayside amenities (NHLML/NHAI PPP model): company says it has been bidding on controlled-access corridors; cash outflow not disclosed. Government reports 501 awarded and 94 operational as of April 2025, with more than 700 expected by FY29.
Ropeway (Parvatmala) opportunities under evaluation as an EPC and operations play; no quantified plan given.
Renewable/EV charging EPC: two EV charging projects commissioned in Indore; more being scoped.

demand_pricing: EPC bid pipeline INR 300-400 crore; win rate approximately 20-25%.
EPC policy: will not go below about 13-14% gross profit; industry peers may bid below 10%.
Toll: company says traffic grows 5-7% annually (up to 10% on some corridors). MLFF rollout seen as limited near-term impact; management views it as positive for PPP-based operators.
Toll strategy is pan-India and not concentrated in one region; regions cited as strong include Andhra Pradesh, Rajasthan, Gujarat, Delhi-NCR and Uttar Pradesh.
Two toll projects were declined or exited on commercial grounds: Venkatapalam (withdrawn, penalty INR 26.33 lakh) and Katiyara (handed over, Bihar).

qa_highlights.question: How does HIL differentiate itself in winning large EPC and toll contracts while protecting profitability?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited pan-India toll coverage, in-house technology for revenue monitoring and leakage control, and an EPC floor of about 13-14% GP, with selective bidding.

qa_highlights.question: What is the potential impact of MLFF tolling on the toll business and how will it be mitigated?
qa_highlights.answer: Management views MLFF as positive: it is PPP-based, lowers operator risk, lengthens tenure and reduces competition; no mitigation planned as it sees no issue. Company is studying MLFF opportunities.

qa_highlights.question: How will the order book convert to revenue in FY27 and FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO-level answer gave FY27 at INR 900 crore (EPC 200, toll 700) and FY28 at INR 1,200 crore (EPC 300, toll 900). Later, FY27 was stated as INR 950 crore (EPC about 300, toll 650).

qa_highlights.question: What are the economics of wayside amenities, including cash outgo, break-even and funding?
qa_highlights.answer: Cash outflow not quantified; break-even 5-8 years on 30-year and about 3-7 years on 20-year contracts; balance sheet said to be supportive, with timing undecided.

qa_highlights.question: Why did receivables rise, and is it one-off?
qa_highlights.answer: Receivables about INR 65 crore, of which INR 27 crore was billed in March and is realisable within three months; management called it a timing issue, to clear within six months.

qa_highlights.question: What are the EPC pipeline, win rate and FY27 revenue guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Pipeline INR 300-400 crore with 20-25% win rate; FY27 guidance INR 950 crore (EPC about 300, toll about 650).

qa_highlights.question: Can margins improve above the FY26 level of about 8% in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to quantify; cited software-driven reductions in site manpower and leakage. Said improvements are a longer-term, continuous process.

544479|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 revenue fell to INR145.8 crore (from INR148.2 crore) on West Asia disruptions, while gross margin rose to 41.9% and EBITDA margin was 14.8%.
544479|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue declined year-on-year as late-March supply and port disruptions linked to the West Asia crisis pushed shipments into April, with management citing a 10-15% shift in volumes. Gross margin improved to 41.9% on a better product, customer and export/domestic mix, and EBITDA was INR21.6 crore (14.8%) with PAT of INR9.4 crore (6.4%). For FY26 revenue grew 9.4% to INR610.4 crore, but EBITDA margin compressed to 14.8% and PAT fell to INR35.6 crore from INR47.3 crore as new Khatalwada capacity and employee costs weighed. Management expects FY27 margins to be better than FY26 with H2 improvement, but Q1 faces a temporary margin hit as price increases of 20-25% are only partly accepted by customers (10-12%).

544479|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 revenue rose 10.5% QoQ to INR161 crore, but gross margin fell 240 bps to 39.5% and EBITDA margin to 14.3% on polymer cost spikes.
544479|2026-06.overview: Revenue reached INR161 crore (up 10.5% QoQ, up 2% YoY) and polymers processed rose 25% QoQ to 6,323 MT, with utilisation at 64.9%. Raw material costs rose 40-50% from the West Asia crisis, compressing gross margin to 39.5% from 41.9%, with price pass-through partial and time-lagged. Management says the pass-through is largely complete in domestic and is contracted for most exports, with the largest customer's benefit landing in Q2 FY27. Supply-chain disruption (inbound material, containers, logistics) was the main drag, with about INR5.5 crore of sales slipping into July.

Khatalwada expansion has raised fixed costs; management says these will be absorbed as utilisation improves.

Management says demand and forecasts have held; supply availability, logistics and raw material inbound were the constraints in April-May, with June improving.
Competition: management views smaller unorganised players under working-capital stress as an opening; large retailers are increasingly focusing on brand and packaging quality.

qa_highlights.question: Is the remaining 4,000 MT capacity delayed and what is the domestic growth driver?

544480|2026-03.headline: JSW Cement Q4 FY26 operating EBITDA rose 46% YoY to INR365 crore (19.3% margin), helped by a one-time INR211 crore deferred tax benefit lifting PAT to INR362 crore.
544480|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue rose 11% YoY to INR1,895 crore on 3.99 million tons of sales volume (+7%), with cement realisation up 4.8% QoQ to INR4,673/ton. Operating EBITDA reached INR916/ton, but GGBS volumes grew only 5.4% YoY due to a slag supply disruption at Dolvi and RMC site closures in Western India. The Nagaur (Rajasthan) plant began commercial operations on 30 March 2026, and management trimmed the Punjab plan in favour of a 2.5 MTPA grinding unit at Nagaur. April demand was soft, though management says volumes are recovering from mid-May.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade

544485|2026-06.headline: Regaal Q1 FY27 operating income fell 18% YoY to Rs 202.15 cr as trading was cut, while value-added margin rose to 39.8% and PAT grew 47% to Rs 13.33 cr.
544485|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 was a transition quarter: the doubled crushing capacity (825 to 1,650 TPD) was commissioned on 26 May 2026, with operations ramping from early June. Operating income fell 18% YoY to Rs 202.15 cr because low-margin trading was deliberately reduced (3.3% of revenue vs 19.5% in Q1 FY26). Value-added revenue grew 30.3% to Rs 80.53 cr and EBITDA rose 26.6% to Rs 30.98 cr, with margin up 540 bps to 15.3%. Capacity utilisation was 71.4%, with management guiding to progressive improvement from Q2 FY27 and a shift to deleveraging after the capex cycle.

segments.name: Trading
segments.commentary: Contribution fell to 3.3% of revenue in Q1 FY27 from 19.5% in Q1 FY26 as low-margin trading was deliberately cut.

segments.name: Value-added products (liquid glucose, maltodextrin, starches)
segments.commentary: Value-added revenue Rs 80.53 cr (+30.3% YoY) at 39.8% margin. Liquid glucose at about 70% of its capacity; maltodextrin powder still ramping, with 2-3 more months needed to reach target.

segments.name: Maize starch / core crushing
segments.commentary: Crushing of 69,689 MT in Q1, with about 5,500 MT of incremental volume attributed by management to liquid glucose and a small part maltodextrin.

guidance_outlook: FY27 crushing expected at about 4 lakh tons (minimum), vs about 2.65 lakh tons in FY26.
Q2 FY27 crushing guided to 100,000-110,000 tons, contingent on smooth stabilisation and integration.
Value-added share of turnover expected at about 20-22% in FY27 (vs about 3% last year); later guided to about 30-35% of turnover on capacity mix.
Management declined to give EBITDA per ton or EBITDA margin guidance, citing maize and product price dependence; said operating leverage and value-add mix should improve margins at constant prices.
Net interest cost (net of subvention) for FY27 expected at about Rs 39-40 crore, broadly flat vs FY26.
Total project outlay about Rs 664 crore, of which about Rs 552 crore incurred as of 30 June 2026.
Working capital debt expected to decline in H2; management cited a prior pattern of about 40% reduction by Q4.
Dextrose Anhydrous, Dextrose Monohydrate and Hydrol expected by about Q4 FY27; modified starches (cationic, carboxymethyl, pre-gel, spray) trials to be fully online by September 2026.
No new capex decided; management said focus is on stabilising at 90-95% utilisation and deleveraging before considering next expansion.
capex_capacity: Crushing capacity doubled from 825 to 1,650 MT per day, commissioned 26 May 2026; operations started early June; described as largest maize wet milling facility in eastern India.
New liquid glucose facility 180 TPD, maltodextrin powder facility 50 TPD, captive cogeneration expanded from 7.1 MW to 15.8 MW.
Q1 utilisation 71.4%; about 9 shutdown days during April-May integration cost roughly 7,200 MT of output (management estimate).
Planned additions: 50,000 MT storage across two new silos, a 50,000 sq ft maize godown, and a 1.6 MW methane gas-based power plant.
Bihar interest subvention applies to new capex debt; management said the subvention cap was amended to Rs 40 crore but final policy notification was still awaited.
demand_pricing: Management said export share rose to 10.4% and that new markets in South and West India are being developed; no export target given.
Pricing: management said starch margin is a whole-number (per-ton) business rather than percentage-based; a rise in starch prices would not proportionally lift EBITDA per ton.
Maize procurement: about 80% of annual requirement bought in the Rabi season (Apr-Jul), 10-15% from other states; Bihar maize quoted at about Rs 22.5-23/kg delivered vs market talk of Rs 24.
Liquid glucose sold mainly September to March; big MNC customers now billed directly, and white-labelling customer base has grown.
About 70-80% of new modified starch volumes expected to go to existing paper-mill and food customers.

qa_highlights.question: What utilisation is the expanded plant running at and when will it reach a comfortable run rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said utilisation is rising from the early-June start and expects maximum utilisation within the year; FY27 crushing expected above 4 lakh tons vs about 2.65 lakh tons in FY26.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 47% PAT jump driven by raw material cost or operating leverage?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it mainly to operating leverage and the drop in low-margin trading from about 19% to about 3% of turnover.

qa_highlights.question: What sustainable EBITDA per ton should be expected in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to guide, citing maize and product price dependence; it expects per-ton EBITDA to improve with scale and value-add at constant prices (Q1 EBITDA/ton cited as about Rs 4,450 vs Rs 4,742 FY26).

qa_highlights.question: What is the net interest cost for FY27 after Bihar subvention?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said about Rs 39-40 crore, broadly flat vs FY26; subvention runs across multiple project loans, with the Rs 40 crore cap still pending final policy.

qa_highlights.question: When will peak debt occur and when will working capital come down?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said debt is peaking in H1 FY27 because working capital is highest then; debt expected to fall in H2.

qa_highlights.question: What production was lost in Q1 and is the value-added capacity stable?
qa_highlights.answer: About 9 shutdown days (approx. 7,200 MT lost). Liquid glucose at about 70% of capacity; maltodextrin needs 2-3 more months; modified starch trials to be online by September.

qa_highlights.question: Any new capex plans for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: No; management wants to stabilise at 90-95% utilisation and reduce debt before considering the next expansion.

risks_watch: Ramp-up risk: Q1 utilisation was 71.4% after about 9 shutdown days (about 7,200 MT lost); Q2 crushing guided to 100,000-110,000 tons and FY27 to at least 4 lakh tons, and both depend on smooth stabilisation and integration.
Maltodextrin powder still needs 2-3 more months to reach target; modified starch trials are to be fully online by September 2026 and dextrose products are expected by about Q4 FY27.
Working capital and leverage: cash conversion cycle at 130 days, net debt Rs 735.32 crore, and debt expected to peak in H1 FY27 before falling in H2.

Interest subvention: the Bihar subvention cap was reportedly amended to Rs 40 crore, but the final policy notification was still awaited; the Rs 20 crore cap is still the one being applied in accounts.
Margin visibility: management declined to guide EBITDA per ton or margin, citing maize and product price dependence, so FY27 margin trajectory remains unquantified.
Maize price exposure: Bihar maize quoted at about Rs 22.5-23/kg versus market talk of Rs 24, with about 80% of annual requirement already bought in the Rabi season.
key_quotes: Q1 FY’27 was a quarter of transition.
So, what we can definitely guide is that we are going to grow our production and we will get operating leverage.
Sustainable at the moment, I cannot tell you, because we are at a time of transition.
It’s too early for us to talk about another next expansion. We are just stabilizing this one.

Specific figures were given on crushing volumes, net interest cost and value-added share, while several answers (subvention amount, starch price trend, product margins) were deferred to the IR team.

rows.why: FY27 crushing guided at 4 lakh tons minimum vs about 2.65 lakh tons in FY26 (+50%), Q2 guided at 100,000-110,000 tons vs 69,689 MT in Q1, though contingent on stabilisation.

rows.why: Management said no new capex decided and wants to stabilise at 90-95% utilisation (Q1 at 71.4%) and deleverage (net debt Rs 735.32 cr) before the next expansion; only planned additions are silos, godown and 1.6 MW methane plant already in plan.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Q1 PAT up 47% to Rs 13.33 cr and export share up to 10.4% from 4.9%, but management gave no revenue or margin upgrade and Q1 operating income fell 18%.

rows.why: Ramp-up risk: 9 shutdown days cost about 7,200 MT, Q1 utilisation 71.4%, maltodextrin still 2-3 months from target, and maize at Rs 22.5-23/kg vs Rs 24 market talk; Q2 guidance depends on smooth stabilisation.

rows.label: Working capital and debt peak then decline
rows.why: CFO said debt peaks in H1 FY27 as working capital is highest, with working capital debt expected to fall in H2 (management cited a prior ~40% reduction by Q4); net debt is Rs 735.32 cr and CCC is 130 days.

rows.why: Subvention cap reportedly amended to Rs 40 cr but final notification awaited; accounts still apply Rs 20 cr cap; FY27 net interest guided at Rs 39-40 cr, flat vs FY26.

rows.why: Export share of revenue rose to 10.4% from 4.9% in Q1 FY26, and management says new markets in South and West India are being developed, though no export target was given.

544487|2026-03.headline: Patel Retail Q4 FY26 PAT rose 39.07% YoY to INR9.98 crore on 53.35% higher income, but EBITDA margin fell to 6.70% as new-store costs hit.
544487|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 total income rose 53.35% YoY to INR339.55 crore, with EBITDA up 31.21% to INR22.74 crore and PAT up 39.07% to INR9.98 crore. FY26 total income crossed INR1,000 crore at INR1,059.29 crore (+28.25%), with PAT up 54.48% to INR39.05 crore and PAT margin at 3.69%. Management attributed the weak Q4 EBITDA margin to upfront costs of new stores and said revenue ramp-up would come in FY27. Analyst questions focused on falling same-store sales (~5%), gross margin compression, a sizeable other-income (FX gain) contribution, and inventory and receivables build-up; several answers were incomplete or inconsistent.

segments.name: Retail
segments.commentary: 51 stores after Rasayani opening in April 2026 (over 2.29 lakh sq ft); 50th store at Thakurli in Q4. Retail sales INR429 crore in FY26; management cited retail EBITDA margin of 7-8% and gross margin of 14-15%, and retail contributes about 35-38% of PAT excluding other income.

segments.name: Manufacturing and processing (B2B)
segments.commentary: Ambernath and Kutch capacity over 1.47 lakh MTPA; utilisation 50-55% vs 45-48% earlier. Management cited about INR618 crore manufacturing and processing sales in FY26, of which about INR319 crore exports; gross margin guided at 16-17% (FY27: 18-20%). Management put manufacturing EBITDA margin at roughly 6.5-7%.

segments.name: Private label / own brands
segments.commentary: Own brands (Indian Chaska, Patel Fresh, Blue Nation, Patel Essentials) are about 17.5% of retail sales; own brands reportedly carry 30-35% operating margins per management, with non-branded gross margin of 15-16%. Indian Chaska distribution covers six states, with MP and Delhi in progress.

guidance_outlook: FY27 EBITDA margin guided at approximately 8-9%.
Gross margin guided at 15-20% overall; FY27 mix expected at 18-20% for B2B and 15-16% for retail.
Management expects double-digit revenue growth in FY27, with 'higher side' at 20% and above, but declined to disclose numbers formally.
Plans to open 8-10 stores a year, with focus on western suburbs and PCMC; possible Gujarat entry. Management said 52 stores as of the call date and seven or eight more expected in FY27.
Management expects positive operating cash flow by H1 FY27 as inventory normalises.
Management expects PAT margin to increase, and expects manufacturing utilisation to rise.
capex_capacity: Manufacturing capacity at Ambernath and Kutch exceeds 1.47 lakh MTPA; utilisation 50-55%, up 4-5 percentage points.
Retail network 51 stores, over 2.29 lakh sq ft; management carries about INR2,000-2,500 inventory per sq ft at store level.
Distribution centre in the cluster holds an additional INR15-20 crore of inventory per management.
Plans to start whole spices in the month of the call, then seasonings, pastes, snacks, and noodles or pasta depending on distribution.
Automation investment planned to improve productivity and cost efficiency.
demand_pricing: Same-store sales growth around 5%; management said mature stores grow 5-6%, versus analyst's recollection of 8-10%.
Grocery and staples are about 68-70% of retail revenue.
Export order book held at INR50-100 crore per management; current export order book figure not provided on the call.
Exports to Sri Lanka, Middle East, Europe, US, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, with African markets being pursued; management says 35+ countries.
Other income of about INR5 crore in Q4 is mainly FX gain on export receivables; management said INR8-9 crore per year is typical and expected to keep rising.
Management said commodity prices have peaked and are declining, and expects inventory gains from raw material procured at competitive prices.

qa_highlights.question: Why did same-store sales appear to slow from 8-10% to about 5%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 5% is good for mature stores, cited no specific reason, and said most revenue comes from grocery and staples (68-70%).

qa_highlights.question: Why did inventory and working capital rise so much?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said incremental working capital was funded from IPO proceeds (INR115 crore deployed into working capital). Management also cited export order book, transit times, and mixed shipments; the exact export order book was not disclosed on the call.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the Q4 margin decline and gross margin fall from about 20% to 14.5%?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO attributed Q4 margin pressure to upfront costs of new stores, and said it is temporary. He did not separately quantify the gross margin decline; management said the West Asia situation had not been the primary factor.

qa_highlights.question: What is the nature of the other income and is it recurring?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said other income is mainly FX gain on export receivables, about INR8-9 crore a year, and expected to keep rising. Management did not explain why the Q4 figure was about INR5 crore or why the gain would be recurring.

qa_highlights.question: Why is retail inventory at about INR90 crore, above the INR55-58 crore implied by store-level inventory per sq ft?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the difference reflects a cluster distribution centre (INR15-20 crore) and category-level inventory days, including about three months of spices stock and three to four months for plastic and steel, with festive stock also included.

qa_highlights.question: Why did receivables rise from INR125 crore to INR161-162 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said about 90% of receivables are less than six months old. He did not explain the increase.

risks_watch: Same-store sales growth of about 5% versus the 8-10% the analyst cited previously; management did not give a clear reason for the slowdown.
Gross margin fell sharply in Q4 (analyst cited about 14.5% versus about 20% a year earlier); management has not quantified the cause.
Other income (FX gain) of about INR5 crore in Q4 is a large share of PAT growth; the analyst argued that excluding it would show a decline.
Inventory (INR259-260 crore) and receivables (INR161-162 crore) rose sharply; management guided to positive operating cash flow only by H1 FY27.
Middle East and West Asia disruption may hit export volumes; management said it is pushing domestic sales to compensate.
DGFT wheat flour export scheme is policy-dependent; management said it does not rely on it fully.
Several Q&A answers were inconsistent or incomplete, including the export order book, the margin split between B2B and B2C, and the retail gross margin figures.

544487|2026-06.headline: Patel Retail Q1 FY27 total income rose 69.35% YoY to INR310.24 crores, but EBITDA margin fell to about 6.3% on raw material intensity.
544487|2026-06.overview: Total income reached INR310.24 crores, up 69.35% YoY from INR183.19 crores, while EBITDA grew 23.92% to INR19.68 crores and PAT rose 37.43% to INR9.52 crores (EPS INR2.85). Management attributed the margin compression (about 133 bps decline cited, and a 233 bps figure also mentioned) to a higher raw-material-intensity mix in manufacturing, export and commodity-linked business amid volatile raw material prices and odd order timing. The company added stores at Rasayani and Babgaon in Q1 and opened its 53rd store at Uran (Raigad) after quarter-end, and expanded Indian Chaska into Madhya Pradesh. Management guided to positive operating cash flow by H1 FY27 and 8 to 10 new stores in FY27.

financial_highlights.change: +69.35% YoY vs INR183.19 crores in Q1 FY26
decline of 133 bps as stated (233 bps also cited in same answer)

financial_highlights.value: around INR101 crores (as referenced by analyst)

financial_highlights.metric: Private label contribution to retail sales

segments.name: Retail (Patel R-Mart)
segments.commentary: 53 stores after Uran opening; average monthly sales per store put at INR80 lakh to INR1 crore, mature-store sales about INR20,000 per sq ft; ticket size INR500 to INR1,000; wastage below 0.1%. Payback about 24 months.

segments.name: Manufacturing / food processing
segments.commentary: Utilisation currently 50% to 55%, targeted at around 80% to 82% by FY27-FY28; automation expected to cut labour cost and improve quality consistency. Private label share of domestic sales cited at 45%, export sales at 37%.

segments.name: Exports and B2B
segments.commentary: Management stated about 40% of revenue from exports and rest from manufacturing and retail; export contribution to bottom line cited as 35% to 40%. These figures were not reconciled in the call.

segments.commentary: Expanded to Madhya Pradesh in August 2026, taking presence to eight states and one union territory; MP averaging INR10 lakh to INR12 lakh per month; whole spices category to be added this quarter.

segments.name: Online / quick commerce
segments.commentary: App has more than 50,000 downloads but online sales were around INR50 lakh in Q1; private label not yet listed on Blinkit or Zepto, with per-SKU terms being finalised; pilot quick commerce running from first stores.

segments.name: Apparel and fashion (general merchandise)
segments.commentary: 8% to 9% of revenue; inventory holding period 15 to 20 days.

qa_highlights.question: What must improve to move EBITDA margin from about 6.3% back to 8% to 9%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 decline was due to higher raw material intensity in manufacturing, export and commodity-linked mix and volatile raw material prices; it expects improvement in coming quarters and not treating Q1 as steady state.

qa_highlights.question: Positive operating cash flow by H1 FY27 still on track, and working capital outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said Q1 balance sheet and cash flow not yet published; expects much better operating cash flow by H1, converting FY26 current-asset build into cash.

qa_highlights.question: How many new stores in FY27 and revenue contribution?
qa_highlights.answer: 8 to 10 stores by FY27, expected to contribute around INR1 crore per month in revenue.

qa_highlights.question: Current utilisation and target?
qa_highlights.answer: Current utilisation 50% to 55%; targeted around 80% to 82% in the medium term, by end-FY27 to FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Share of own brands across channels?
qa_highlights.answer: Own brands about 17.5% of overall revenue; private label 17.55% of retail sales, 37% of export sales and 45% of domestic sales as stated by the CFO.

qa_highlights.question: Performance of recently opened stores vs older stores?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said new stores are operationally breakeven since day one, with some growing strongly; payback target about 24 months.

Online and quick commerce traction remains small (about INR50 lakh in Q1) and competition from platform in-house brands noted by analysts.

544491|2026-06.headline: Gem Aromatics Q1 FY27 standalone revenue rose to INR83 crore (from INR76 crore) but consolidated EBITDA fell to INR3.3 crore (3.3% margin) and consolidated PAT was a INR7.9 crore loss.

Margins compressed on product mix, clove raw-material costs after Madagascar floods, and a higher fixed cost base at the new Dahej plant. Consolidated PAT was a loss of INR7.9 crore, pressured by INR9.1 crore of higher depreciation after capitalisation of most of the INR270 crore Dahej capex. Management says the new verticals (cooling agents, Safranal/Citral, phenol derivatives) start contributing from Q2 to Q4 FY27, with FY27 framed as a ramp-up year and no guidance given.

qa_highlights.question: How will the business reach sustainable consolidated profitability?

544495|2026-03.headline: NIS Management Q4 FY26 consolidated income rose 13.96% to INR180.03 crore; FY26 PAT hit by INR27.82 crore labour-code provision, adjusted PAT INR19.12 crore.

544495|2026-06.headline: NIS Management Q1 FY27 consolidated income rose 15.68% YoY to INR115.44 crore, with EBITDA up 36.24% to INR9.22 crore at a 7.99% margin.

544496|2026-03.headline: Vikran FY26 revenue hit a record INR1,249 crore (vs INR916 crore) with EBITDA margin near 14%; FY27 guided at INR2,200 crore plus.
544496|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue from operations was INR647 crore, up from INR355 crore a year earlier, with EBITDA of INR92 crore (14.2% margin) and PAT of INR56 crore (vs INR38 crore). For FY26, revenue rose to INR1,249 crore, EBITDA was about INR175 crore (around 14%) and PAT was INR92 crore (vs about INR78 crore). Management attributed margin dilution to delayed Jal Jeevan Mission receivables (provisioned, mostly in Q4), and to early-stage solar EPC projects. The company closed its acquisition of NOPL Solar (969 MW PM-KUSUM project) at end-April 2026 and guided FY27 revenue of INR2,200 crore plus, with a 14-15% EBITDA margin target.

rows.why: FY27 standalone execution target is INR2,200-2,500 crores against a INR6,496 crore order book, with NOPL revenue of about INR1,500 crores planned (about INR100 crores in September, about INR1,400 crores in H2), though the schedule is described as conservative with slippage risk; Q1 standalone revenue was INR204 crores, up 28.2% YoY.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Management is putting up capex so power can be sold to the state DISCOM, with the NOPL project cost about INR4,000 crores (debt about INR3,100 crores), IREDA final sanction and disbursement expected in Q2 FY27, and a CFA subsidy of about INR1,017 crores as backup.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: The FY27 revenue guide of INR2,300-2,500 crores is new and depends on H2 NOPL execution, with Q1 standalone revenue of INR204 crores and management attributing the weak H1 to seasonality and client budget constraints.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: NOPL needs about INR1,400 crores of revenue in H2 against a conservative schedule with possible quarter-to-quarter slippage, debtor days at 296 (peak per CFO), and NOPL debt financing not yet sanctioned; consolidated PAT of INR4 crores vs standalone INR17.5 crores adds to the risk.

rows.label: Data centre first order
rows.why: Quotes made with consultant E&Y and a target of at least one order by end FY27, but management was vague on revenue potential and no order is in hand yet.

rows.label: Debtor days improvement
rows.why: Debtor days at 296 are described by the CFO as the peak, with about INR23 crores of JJM receipts last quarter and more than INR10 crores in the last 30 days against about INR120 crores of JJM debtors.

rows.label: Cash positive by end FY27
rows.why: Management committed to cash positive by end FY27 if 650 MW of NOPL solar is commissioned, which depends on IREDA disbursement in Q2 and on the commissioning pace.

tone.note: Management was confident on execution, the 14%-17% margin band, and NOPL timelines, but defensive on the standalone-versus-consolidated revenue gap and deflected detailed margin questions; analysts pressed on low H1 revenue, debtor days at 296, the INR29 crore court dispute and NOPL financing.

544497|2026-03.headline: Anlon FY26 consolidated income rose 42.98% to INR 172.22 crore and PAT 41.77% to INR 29.09 crore, but Q4 PAT fell to INR 11.07 crore from INR 16.65 crore.
544497|2026-03.overview: Management reported FY26 consolidated total income of INR 172.22 crore (+42.98% YoY), EBITDA of INR 47.77 crore (+47.55%) and PAT of INR 29.09 crore (+41.77%), driven by the Apiqo and Bizotic acquisitions. Q4 total income rose to INR 50.90 crore from INR 48.97 crore, but PBT was flat at INR 14.44 crore and PAT fell to INR 11.07 crore, which management attributed to higher operating and development expenses and raw material cost spikes linked to the Middle East conflict. Management guided FY27 revenue to INR 380-400 crore, FY28 to INR 700-800 crore in one answer (INR 600-700 crore in another), and consolidated EBITDA margin of 24-25% as a floor, with a sharp reduction in receivables and cash-flow positivity targeted by end FY27. Several answers were inconsistent (EBITDA margin guidance ranged from 24-25% to 30-35%; FY28 revenue from 600-700 to 700-800 crore), and the call was disrupted by poor audio for several analysts.

vs INR 16.65 crore in Q4 FY25

segments.name: Pharmaceutical intermediates and APIs (Anlon standalone)
segments.commentary: Management says 5-6 DMF-linked products are already supplied to regulated markets, with 5-7 more expected to commercialise in FY27; export share targeted at about 60% in FY27. Products cited include Ketoprofen, Dexketoprofen and Loxoprofen Sodium in the NSAID category.

segments.name: Apiqo Organics (acquired, early Jan 2026 per management)
segments.commentary: Acquired and consolidated for about 2.5 months in FY26. Management said its EBITDA margin is structurally lower (approx. 22-23%) as a chemical/intermediate manufacturer, and backward integration into intermediates is planned to start from Q2 FY27.

segments.name: Bizotic Life Science (acquired)
segments.commentary: Consolidated for about 15 days in FY26. Management expects margins close to Anlon's, and says backward integration of intermediates has run for three to four years.

segments.commentary: Early-traction vertical; management is discussing a dedicated Apiqo capacity expansion with one or two customers, with margins slightly below pharma. No revenue figure was disclosed.

segments.name: CDMO
segments.commentary: Three molecules in development for two global innovators. One is in validation with batches of hundreds of kg since March; commercial supply expected by Q3 FY27, with the other two in validation by Q2 FY27.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue guided at INR 380-400 crore, with a clear order book of INR 280-300 crore and a further INR 80-90 crore expected from products under qualification.
FY28 revenue guided at INR 700-800 crore in one answer and INR 600-700 crore in another, assuming 50-60% utilisation of the new Rajkot capacity from Q1 FY28 (six months of trial and validation).

Consolidated EBITDA margin guided at 24-25% as a floor, with management saying it will not sell below levels that breach that margin; a separate answer cited 30-35% for FY27 and the closing remarks used 25-30%.
Consolidated PAT: conservative FY27 estimate of INR 45 crore; management agreed INR 50-55 crore is achievable when asked.
Operating cash flow expected to turn positive on an annual basis by end FY27; management said it was '100% sure'.
Revenue CAGR of approx. 30% over three years stated in prepared remarks; peak revenue potential of the current 1,400-1,600 MTPA capacity stated at INR 450-500 crore at 80% utilisation.
capex_capacity: Combined installed capacity after Apiqo and Bizotic: approx. 1,400-1,600 MTPA; consolidated utilisation approx. 62-65%, with management saying practical maximum is about 85%.

New greenfield capex at the existing Rajkot premises estimated at INR 130 crore; plant layout under approval, construction to start end of the month or early next month, commercial production targeted by Q1 FY28 (also referred to as mid-FY28).

Funding: term loan of INR 65-70 crore (about 50-60% of capex), balance from internal accruals; equipment orders placed 6-8 months ahead, with advance payments already made and part of the equipment installed.
Standalone peak revenue with expansion stated at INR 400-450 crore.
Capex and expansion of QC capacity already under way; management is considering a further INR 130 crore-type expansion to scale specialty chemicals at Apiqo, subject to customer commitments.
demand_pricing: Management said raw material prices (solvents, catalysts) have more than doubled since the conflict, and prices change daily; Q4 margin pressure came from holding purchase orders at old prices, and customers are now being asked to pay higher prices as a force majeure.
Management said price increases are being negotiated and expects Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin to be close to the prior full-year level, but acknowledged this is uncertain if geopolitical conditions worsen.

Ketoprofen US DMF is delayed: a customer will file on Anlon's behalf, and timing has moved from Q2 FY27 to Q3 or Q4 FY27. Dexketoprofen Europe DMF is at the EDQM query stage, expected to close in two to three months.

Competitive positioning: few Indian players in Ketoprofen and Dexketoprofen (two to three in India, five to six globally); management cites proprietary methylation and Friedel-Crafts chemistry and landing-cost advantage.

Receivables: a distributor dispute left INR 20-30 crore pending in late 2025; INR 11 crore recovered and about INR 17 crore still outstanding. Management has stopped supply to customers paying beyond 120 days.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 revenue outlook and the peak potential of the current capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 visibility is INR 380-400 crore; peak revenue from 1,400-1,600 MTPA is INR 450-500 crore at about 80% utilisation (management said the practical ceiling is 85%).

qa_highlights.question: How much order book is in place and what are the CDMO timelines?
qa_highlights.answer: Clear order book is INR 280-300 crore, with INR 80-90 crore more expected. One CDMO product is in validation, with commercial supply expected by Q3 FY27; the other two validations by Q2 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is the EBITDA margin outlook, and why did Q4 fall?
qa_highlights.answer: Management guided consolidated margin of 24-25% as a floor; Q4 fell because of unrecovered raw material cost increases, higher operating costs and the acquisitions. Management expects Q1 FY27 margins to recover to roughly the prior full-year level.

qa_highlights.question: What is the funding plan for the capex, working capital and any acquisitions?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex is funded with INR 65-70 crore of term loans and internal accruals; management said there is no current equity dilution plan, with rights issue or promoter unsecured loans as possible options later. Working capital may need cash credit from banks after commissioning.

qa_highlights.question: What is the receivables outlook and cash-flow timing?
qa_highlights.answer: Receivable days are 130-140 on average, and management expects them to stay at or above 180 days (per one answer), while also saying payments are running at 100-105 days now. Cash flow expected positive on an annual basis in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Credit rating and minority buy-out status?
qa_highlights.answer: CARE's 'issuer not cooperating' rating was linked to a dispute management called blackmail; Brickwork withdrew its rating and a fresh application is pending, with management expecting BBB- minimum within about 45 days. Management plans to acquire the remaining minority stake in Apiqo and Bizotic through share swaps, likely at the next AGM.

Receivables at 130-140 days on average (some 150 days), with management saying they will stay at or above 180 days; cash flow turning positive on an annual basis by end FY27 depends on collections and inventory release of 20-25% in Q2 FY27.

Capex of about INR 130 crore at Rajkot with commercial production targeted Q1 FY28; funding relies on INR 65-70 crore term loan plus internal accruals, with working capital needs possibly requiring cash credit after commissioning.
Credit rating status: CARE rating marked 'issuer not cooperating' and Brickwork withdrew its rating; a fresh application is pending with management expecting BBB- minimum within about 45 days.
Ketoprofen US DMF timing slipped to Q3 or Q4 FY27 through a customer filing; Dexketoprofen Europe DMF at EDQM query stage, expected to close in two to three months.
FY28 revenue guidance differs between INR 600-700 crore and INR 700-800 crore; FY27 PAT conservative INR 45 crore versus INR 50-55 crore said achievable.

But right now there is no planning, but I think once the capacity will be completed and we'll come with the commercial production, at that time we'll see that whatever the situation and if required, then our first preference is go with the financial institution instead of going further for the dilution.
So we are 100% sure by end of this FY27 it will be positive.
And by end of this FY27 with the positive cash flow and receivable days will remain at least 180 days, which is I think mostly API manufacturer is having.

Several answers were evasive or deflected (for example on tax rate, acquisition budget and the reason for the Q4 PAT decline), and the call was hampered by poor audio for several analysts.

544497|2026-06.headline: Anlon Q1 FY27 consolidated EBITDA margin fell to ~17% (PAT ₹8.28 cr) on raw-material spikes and Remember India consolidation; management targets 25-27% for FY27.
544497|2026-06.overview: Consolidated Q1 FY27 total income was ₹87.62 cr versus ₹33.31 cr in Q1 FY26, with EBITDA of ₹15.65 cr (vs ₹6.26 cr) and PAT of ₹8.28 cr (vs ₹3.55 cr). EBITDA margin moderated to about 17%, which management attributed to a sharp rise in solvent and petrochemical raw-material prices after the geopolitical conflict and to operating costs of the newly acquired Remember India Health links being consolidated. The company completed the 63.98% acquisition of Remember India on 8 May 2026, has acquired Apiqo Organics and Bizotic Lifesciences, and is moving into finished dosage formulations. Management reiterated FY27 revenue guidance of ₹350-400 cr and a ~30% three-year revenue CAGR, but gave limited quantitative detail on Remember India.

financial_highlights.change: moderated; management earlier guided ~24-25% floor for Q1

financial_highlights.change: management cited standalone sales of ₹30 cr vs ₹33 cr in analyst question

segments.commentary: Q1 revenue ~₹30-32 cr, down from ₹33 cr YoY per analyst; management says it is at peak utilisation and expects FY27 standalone revenue of ~₹180 cr. Production cycles of 30-45 days mean some output lands in Q2.

segments.name: Apiqo Organics (68% stake, moving to 100%)
segments.commentary: Q1 revenue ~₹45 cr, described as the most profitable unit; FY27 revenue expected ₹120-150 cr. Business is fully booked in industrial and fine chemicals; share-swap to make it a 100% subsidiary to complete by end-Q2.

segments.name: Bizotic Lifesciences (57% stake, moving to 100%)
segments.commentary: Q1 revenue ~₹12 cr; FY27 expected ~₹60 cr. Management says it is profitable and that committed partner business exists; share-swap to 100% also targeted by end-Q2.
