segments.commentary: Finished dosage formulations (tablets, capsules, ointments) with access to 30+ dossiers; in investment and turnaround phase. No revenue assumed for FY27 until at least Q4 FY27; WHO-PQ approval expected by end-CY2026. Margin expected above 25%.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue guidance of ₹350-400 cr reiterated; management said H1 comparison is the right lens, and the guidance range was re-confirmed as ₹380-400 cr in one answer.
EBITDA margin: ~17% in Q1; management expects margins to improve from Q2 (said 'better than the first quarter') and target 25-27% for FY27 on consolidated basis; earlier comment of 22-25% in H1.
Gross margin expected to hold at 40-45%.
FY28 revenue indicated at ~₹700 cr if Anlon-site expansion (~₹130 cr capex, ~1,200 MT additional) is commissioned on schedule by Q1 FY28; management flagged possible delays from statutory approvals.

Working capital: receivable days expected to fall toward 60-70 days over time (current ~130-135 days vs 90-day terms); management expects positive operating cash flow in FY27, 'lower but positive'. Management also said H1 operating cash flow positive is targeted before year-end.
Biologics subsidiary (Anlon Biologics) revenue expected from Q4 FY28; Anlon Medicare from Q2 FY28; Remember India peak revenue/EBITDA to be detailed in Q2 call.
capex_capacity: Installed capacity after three acquisitions stated at ~1,400-1,600 MT per annum; management clarified Anlon standalone is ~400 MT and is at peak.
Anlon-site expansion: ~₹130 cr capex adding ~1,200 MT (standalone to ~1,600 MT); commissioning targeted by Q1 FY28 subject to statutory approvals.
Funding: ~₹70 cr debt at ~8.5-8.6% interest; balance from internal accruals.
Eight new cleanrooms planned at the new facility to run eight APIs in parallel; initial planning assumes 50-60% utilisation.
Bizotic and Apiqo utilisation can rise gradually from ~65% toward higher levels; no 65-to-85% jump expected within this year.
Anlon Biologics (peptides, biosimilars) construction to begin within ~2 months; in-house peptide manufacturing targeted by FY28.
demand_pricing: Raw material prices: management said solvent/methanol-linked inputs rose 2-3x since pre-war (methanol cited at ₹22 to ₹58-60/kg); not yet normalised. Around 40% of API manufacturing cost is solvents and petroleum-linked inputs.

Price pass-through: price increases on finished products have been initiated and customers have agreed; management expects this to reflect over the next one to two quarters, but earlier orders at old prices weighed on Q1.
Customer base is concentrated: 10-15 B2B customers, which limits ability to reprice frequently.
Fine/specialty chemicals (Apiqo): fully booked, described as 'overbooked'; management estimates ₹120-150 cr contribution in FY27.
CDMO: expected commercial supply of first molecule by Q3 and others by Q4 FY27 or Q1 FY28; process validations ongoing.
Seven new APIs/DMFs planned for filing within FY27; compilation under way.

qa_highlights.question: Have raw material prices normalised, and by which quarter will EBITDA margins recover? Will Q2 margins be similar to Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: RM prices not normalised; solvent/methanol-linked inputs up 2-3x (methanol ~₹22 to ₹58-60/kg). Management expects margin normalisation by Q3 and said Q2 would be better than Q1, with price increases reflecting over one to two quarters.

qa_highlights.question: FY27 revenue outlook versus ~₹87 cr Q1 run-rate and capacity utilisation (~62%)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated ₹350-400 cr as peak-level potential and said utilisation is ~65-70%; asked to compare H1 rather than quarter-on-quarter because production cycles run 15-40+ days.

qa_highlights.question: Segment revenue contribution in Q1 and expected FY27 split?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1: Apiqo ~₹45 cr, Anlon standalone ~₹32 cr, Bizotic ~₹11.5-12 cr. FY27 expectations: Apiqo ₹120-150 cr, Anlon standalone ~₹180 cr, Bizotic ~₹60 cr; Remember India not included until Q3/Q4 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Why has EBITDA margin declined over the last two quarters, and what is the FY27 consolidated margin expectation?
qa_highlights.answer: Attributed to temporary geopolitical RM spike with customers on prior-price orders, plus lower-margin acquired units and Remember India costs. Management guided 25-27% consolidated EBITDA for FY27 and said Q2 would sustain around 25%.

qa_highlights.question: Expected Remember India revenue and margin?
qa_highlights.answer: No FY27 revenue assumed; WHO-PQ approval expected by end-CY2026; detailed projection deferred to Q2 call. Management said margins should be above 25% due to in-house API backward integration.

qa_highlights.question: Working capital, receivable days and operating cash flow outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Receivables run ~130-135 days versus 90-day terms; management expects reduction toward 60-70 days over time and 'lower but positive' operating cash flow in FY27, targeted before year-end. Inventory is development stock held 9-12 months pending DMF approval.

qa_highlights.question: Interest rate on the ~₹70 cr debt and PAT margin expectations?
qa_highlights.answer: Debt cost ~8.5-8.6%; PAT margin guided at ~12-13% for FY27 and ~11-13% for FY28, described as conservative and sensitive to statutory approval delays.

risks_watch: Raw material cost: solvent and petrochemical inputs have not normalised; ~40% of API manufacturing cost is solvent/petroleum-linked, so Q2 margin recovery depends on price pass-through taking effect over the next one to two quarters.
Customer concentration: only 10-15 B2B customers, limiting ability to reprice quickly; older orders at old prices weighed on Q1.
Remember India: no FY27 revenue assumed; WHO-PQ approval targeted by end-CY2026; peak revenue and EBITDA to be detailed only in Q2 call.
Capacity expansion: ~₹130 cr Anlon-site capex (~1,200 MT) targeted by Q1 FY28 but subject to statutory approvals; management flagged possible delays of one to two months changing projections.
Working capital and cash flow: receivable days of ~130-135 vs 90-day terms; management suggests a possible fundraise may be needed for the FY28 revenue ambition, which it did not confirm.

Guidance consistency: management gave differing EBITDA margin ranges (25-27%, 25-28%, 25-30%) and revenue framing; watch Q2 for reconciliation and the share-swap completion of Apiqo and Bizotic to 100% by end-Q2.

So, in terms of the percentage, it will remain the same.

544501|2026-03.headline: Sugs Lloyd FY26 revenue rose about 70% to INR300 crore, PAT up 71% to INR28 crore, with INR825 crore unexecuted order book.
544501|2026-03.overview: FY26 revenue reached INR300 crore versus INR176 crore in FY25, ahead of the INR270 crore guidance, with EBITDA up 69% and PAT up 71% to about INR28 crore. Management said margins were held broadly flat year-on-year, though Q4 margin was about 12% versus roughly 14% for the half year, which management attributed to a delayed MAHAGENCO order and related site disruption. Growth drivers were RDSS-funded transmission and distribution work and solar EPC, plus a INR640 crore (incl. 18% GST, about INR540 crore ex-GST) SCADA order from Konkan Railway. Receivables and retention balances rose, and management flagged 40% of FY26 sales coming in Q4 as a key working-capital issue.

544511|2026-03.headline: Karbonsteel crossed ₹300 crore revenue in FY26 with 10.86% EBITDA margin and ₹10.51 crore PAT, which management says normalises to ₹16.56 crore.

The company entered bridal jewellery with Tanishq and Malabar Gold and Diamonds, and management reiterated about 30% value CAGR guidance for the next two to three years. rows.why: Native loss fell to -8.9% of NTV in FY26 from -25.1% in FY25 (₹31 crore vs ₹39 crore), and management is fairly confident of break-even, but gave no timeline.

rows.label: International (UAE + Singapore) and KSA JV profitability
rows.why: International FY26 NTV grew 75% to ₹700 crore with EBITDA turning positive at ₹6 crore, Q4 NTV rose 84% to ₹211 crore despite the March UAE disruption, and the KSA JV shows improving margins with visibility toward profitability.

rows.label: InstaHelp order scale-up
rows.why: InstaHelp did 2.7 million orders and ₹40 crore NTV in Q4, with March alone above 1.1 million orders, though management is not giving quarterly InstaHelp commentary.

tone.note: Management was confident on Core densification, International profitability and the 26% Services ex-InstaHelp growth, but defensive on InstaHelp unit economics, declining to give steady-state or quarterly guidance; analysts pressed on AOV pressure, competitive intensity and the Native break-even tim

544515|2026-06.headline: Urban Company Q1 FY27 consolidated NTV rose 42% YoY to ₹1,465 crore; Services NTV grew 29% and InstaHelp loss narrowed to ₹(132) crore.
544515|2026-06.overview: Consolidated NTV grew 42% YoY to ₹1,465 crore and revenue rose 44% to ₹528 crore, with orders up 79% YoY to 13.2 million. Core Services NTV accelerated for a fourth straight quarter to 29% growth (₹1,056 crore), and Services adjusted EBITDA margin improved to 6.9% of NTV. Consolidated loss was ₹(65) crore, almost entirely from InstaHelp, while the rest of the business delivered an adjusted EBITDA of ₹67 crore. Management retained its guidance of consolidated adjusted EBITDA breakeven by Q3 FY28 and ₹1,000 crore adjusted EBITDA by FY31, and framed InstaHelp as the main investment area.

financial_highlights.change: +5.2 pp YoY (stated as 170 bps improvement in the margin line in the Q&A)
improved from (11.4)% a year ago (410 bps)
Loss per order ₹(346) vs ₹(447) in Q4
1.2 million new customers added in the quarter

segments.name: Core Services
segments.commentary: NTV ₹1,056 crore, growing 29% YoY, the fourth consecutive quarter of acceleration (10%→19%→21%→26%→29%). Adjusted EBITDA margin 6.9% of NTV, up 5.2 pp YoY per the call; management says the 29% base was muted by unseasonal rains and monsoon in the prior year.

segments.name: International
segments.commentary: NTV ₹237 crore, up 76% YoY (58% ex-currency). UAE and Singapore both grew strongly; the Saudi Arabia JV is approaching profitability. UAE and Saudi JV are described as nearing or at profitability, and the company is not planning new international markets.

segments.name: InstaHelp
segments.commentary: NTV ₹119 crore (+51% YoY), net revenue ₹95 crore (+60% YoY); adjusted EBITDA loss ₹(132) crore, or (7.3)% of NTV versus (11.4)% a year ago. Largest investment; management expects it to need 2 or more years of investment and aims for adjusted breakeven within about 18 months.

guidance_outlook: Retains guidance of consolidated adjusted EBITDA breakeven by Q3 FY28.
Retains guidance of ₹1,000 crore adjusted EBITDA by FY31.
Long-term Services adjusted EBITDA margin guidance of 9-10% of NTV; currently at 6.9%. Management said it is not in a rush and sees the target as achievable without trading off growth.
Management said Services will be a cash-generating business going forward and that it intends to keep it profitable; InstaHelp is expected to need 2 years or more of investment.
Management explicitly declined to give growth guidance beyond the 29% trend, saying the company does not want to set the wrong expectations.
Top-15-city TAM for InstaHelp is ₹7,000-12,000 crore NTV annually; management's base case is ₹7,000-8,000 crore and the bull case is ₹10,000-12,000 crore.
capex_capacity: InstaHelp: management said the company is investing aggressively in micro-market density, with the investment level still under evaluation.
Core Services trainer and infrastructure capacity is being scaled up with AI support; management says the company is 'all hands on deck' as supply grows.
Beauty segment: partners are being retrained and retooled, and the company moved to a majority of professionals having access to two-wheelers, with the target of approaching 100%.

Services is expected to consume less capital as InstaHelp is scaled; management said capital allocation will be reviewed once InstaHelp approaches adjusted breakeven (hopefully within about 18 months).
demand_pricing: Management said Q1 was among the best quarters in the company's history, with growth broad-based.

InstaHelp pricing: sustainable professional payout is about ₹130-160 per hour, with ₹150 as the rule of thumb. Management said an AOV of about ₹300 is needed for InstaHelp to break even, with ₹200 per hour required to clear gross breakeven.

Management said competitors in the InstaHelp category have pricing of ₹80-120 per hour for full-month subscriptions and that competitive intensity is high; it said the company has no reason to comment on rival strategies.
Management said the 3 major players have limited their household coverage to about 3.5-4 million households; the company believes most spending goes to subsidised repeat orders.
Management said the company has 'underestimated' the Tier 2 opportunity, with Tier 2 cities performing as well as Tier 1.

Management said it is seeing acceleration in MAUs, DAUs and MTUs, with conversion rates improving; the marketing spend in Services was about ₹25 crore in the quarter versus ₹24 crore a year ago (flat).

qa_highlights.question: Morgan Stanley: is the Cheaper, Faster, Better flywheel now visible enough to call a bold trajectory shift in Services NTV growth, and can growth be guided higher?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the flywheel comes from densifying many micro-markets, which improves partner utilisation, lowers churn and supports trust. It cited UC Instant (30-60 minute service) as a new driver. It declined to give growth guidance, said the 29% was helped by a muted prior-year base from unseasonal rains and monsoon, and said the margin of 6.9% is in line with the 9-10% long-term target, which is not a trade-off against growth.

qa_highlights.question: Morgan Stanley: why should InstaHelp get capital and attention, and how will capital be allocated over two years between Services, new segments and international?
qa_highlights.answer: InstaHelp is strategically relevant because its high frequency keeps users on the app weekly. Services is to be profitable and cash generating; UAE and Singapore are profitable wholly owned subsidiaries; the Saudi JV is nearing profitability. InstaHelp needs two years or more of investment, with capital allocation revisited at adjusted breakeven, hopefully within about 18 months.

qa_highlights.question: Goldman Sachs: why not export the UAE and Saudi model to new international markets, given Core Services is generating cash?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited bandwidth as the main constraint. It said playbooks need local customisation plus some luck, and that earlier Australia and US launches did not succeed. It will stay focused on UAE, Saudi Arabia and India, with no plans for new international markets for now.

qa_highlights.question: Goldman Sachs: where does Services margin go from 6.9% of NTV versus the 9-10% target, and would the company cap margin around 10% or reinvest?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the goal is to reach the 9-10% range without rushing and without trading growth for margin. Priority one is growing fast, priority two is margin expansion. Once it reaches about 10%, it will decide whether to lift margins further or reinvest for faster growth.

qa_highlights.question: Goldman Sachs: is the InstaHelp TAM structurally lower, and would the company operate at a narrow loss if competition leaves room for only two players?
qa_highlights.answer: The base case is INR 7,000-8,000 crore NTV and the bull case is INR 10,000-12,000 crore, with 3 orders per user per month. Management said the 3 major players have limited coverage to about 3.5-4 million households and that subsidised repeat orders dominate spend. It expects a low single-digit market share outcome and says it will not spend heavily on the category to drive share, while being opinionated about winning micro-markets.

qa_highlights.question: Bank of America: what AOV is needed for InstaHelp to break even, and is there scope for growth above 29%?
qa_highlights.answer: Sustainable professional payout is INR 130-160 per hour, with INR 150 as the rule of thumb. Gross breakeven needs about INR 200 per hour, and an AOV of about INR 300 is needed for InstaHelp to break even. Management said breakeven could take a couple of years or up to 5 years, and it declined to give growth guidance beyond the 29%.

qa_highlights.question: Bank of America: how is AI being used and how much margin benefit is there?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 90-95% of the code is now written by AI, and that support, supply-side onboarding, quality audits and fraud detection are increasingly AI-led. Marketing and Finance/HR run AI end-to-end. It said the margin benefit has started to show but there is a long way to go.

qa_highlights.question: Kotak: is Beauty acceleration sustainable, and are the 30-40 annual transactions per user assumption and consolidation prospects realistic?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Beauty has seen a resurgence after retraining and retooling partners, and that the company had underinvested there a couple of years back. Two-wheeler access for Beauty professionals is now a majority. It expects 3 transactions per month, not 30-40, for the 10-12 lakh household case. It expects private players to keep burning cash and believes it will be the eventual winner in the category.

qa_highlights.question: Bellwether: what is driving the 5 lakh quarter-on-quarter user addition, what marketing spend is involved, and what training and capacity constraints exist in InstaHelp and Core Services?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the user growth is largely from MAU, DAU and MTU growth and better conversion, and that marketing spend in Services was about INR 25 crore versus INR 24 crore a year ago. For Core, it said capacity is comfortable but is being scaled up, with all hands on deck, to match trainer and infrastructure growth. It said InstaHelp supply is also being expanded.

qa_highlights.question: Emkay: is the shift to premium products a sign of a premium customer base, and will the company expand beyond water purifiers and smart locks?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said its products, such as the M3 water purifier with a 3-year no-service, no-filter-change design, are aimed at lowering lifecycle cost. It said it is not building a durables company and will keep its focus on a small number of categories, mainly water purifiers and smart locks, with the aim of serving the top households in India.

risks_watch: InstaHelp losses: the loss was INR (132) crore; management expects 2+ years of investment and an adjusted breakeven target within about 18 months. Track loss per order, which improved from INR (447) in Q4 to INR (346) in Q1.
AOV and payout economics: InstaHelp needs about INR 300 AOV to break even, with pay of INR 130-160 per hour; competitor pricing of INR 80-120 per hour is a pressure point.
Competition and TAM: management said 3 major players have limited coverage to 3.5-4 million households; the TAM base case is INR 7,000-8,000 crore against a bull case of INR 10,000-12,000 crore.
Growth sustainability: Services NTV growth of 29% was helped by a muted prior-year base, and management declined to give forward growth guidance.
Services margin: current 6.9% of NTV against a 9-10% long-term target; the timing of expansion remains unspecified.
Capacity and trainer scaling for Core Services as user additions accelerate.
544515|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on the Services growth trend and the balance sheet, but cautious and deliberately non-committal on forward growth, TAM and the timing of InstaHelp breakeven. Management repeatedly declined to set expectations beyond the 29% trend.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Services adjusted EBITDA margin is 6.9% of NTV versus a 9-10% long-term target, and management is 'not in a rush' with growth prioritised; InstaHelp loss narrowed to (7.3)% of NTV from (11.4)% a year ago, and loss per order improved to INR (346) from INR (447) in Q4.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: No new plant or branch capacity quantified; Core Services trainer and infrastructure capacity is being scaled 'all hands on deck' and InstaHelp micro-market density investment is still under evaluation, with capital allocation to be revisited near InstaHelp breakeven (~18 months).

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Total orders rose 79% YoY to 13.2 million, 1.2 million new customers were added, InstaHelp orders grew 43% QoQ to 3.82 million, and Services NTV growth accelerated for a fourth straight quarter to 29%, though management gave no forward growth number.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Management said Services will consume less capital as InstaHelp scales and capital allocation will be reviewed only once InstaHelp nears adjusted breakeven (~18 months); no utilisation metric or capex figure was given.

rows.label: New product launch

rows.label: InstaHelp loss narrowing toward breakeven
rows.why: Adjusted EBITDA loss improved to (7.3)% of NTV from (11.4)% a year ago and loss per order to INR (346) from INR (447) in Q4, but the INR (132) crore quarterly loss persists and management says 2+ years of investment is needed.

rows.label: AI-driven efficiency in Services
rows.why: Management says 90-95% of code is AI-written and support, onboarding, quality audits and fraud detection are increasingly AI-led, with margin benefit started but 'a long way to go' toward the 9-10% target from 6.9%.

rows.label: No new international markets
rows.why: Bandwidth is the main constraint and earlier Australia and US launches failed, so focus stays on UAE, Saudi Arabia and India, where International NTV grew 76% YoY to INR 237 crore.

tone.note: Management was confident on the Services growth trend, the balance sheet and Tier 2 demand, but cautious and non-committal on forward growth, InstaHelp TAM and breakeven timing; analysts pressed on the 6.9% vs 9-10% margin path, InstaHelp AOV economics and competitive pricing.

544515|2026-09.headline: Urban Company's consolidated NTV rose 39.1% to ₹1,432.3 crore in Q2 FY27, with adjusted EBITDA (ex-Native/International investment) at ₹30 crore, up 213% YoY.
544515|2026-09.overview: Management reported Q2 FY27 consolidated NTV up 39.1% YoY to ₹1,432.3 crore and revenue from operations up 41.4% to ₹537.3 crore, with adjusted loss of ₹144 crore after a ₹174 crore investment in Native. Core Services adjusted EBITDA was ₹30 crore ex-investments, and management reiterated breakeven for the consolidated business by Q3 FY28 and a ₹1,000 crore EBITDA-type goal for FY31. Management announced a fundraise of up to ₹2,500 crore, framed as flexibility rather than a need to fund losses. Q&A focused on the rationale for the raise, Native's AC launch, professional supply, and pricing/contribution economics.

financial_highlights.change: +213% YoY; ₹119 crore for trailing four quarters, +175%
vs NTV growth of 26%, per management
up 110 bps (from prior level per call)

segments.name: Core Services (India)
segments.commentary: Management said Core Services adjusted EBITDA was ₹30 crore ex-investments and contribution margin rose to 3.5%; NTV growth was attributed to new-customer acquisition, repeat cohorts and densification, with instant service now used in top 7–8 cities.

segments.name: International (UAE, Saudi, Singapore)
segments.commentary: International NTV grew 66.2% YoY per management, with UAE described as a key market; adjusted EBITDA margin was 2% of NTV, improved by 190 bps. Management said war-related concerns are behind it and Q2+Q3 combined growth is expected at 50–55%.

segments.name: Native (water purifiers / AC services)
segments.commentary: Native's loss narrowed by ₹220 crore (per call) with loss per order down 19% QoQ to ₹279; management says Native is being built deliberately with a ₹174 crore investment in Q2 and is in a learning phase for its first AC device.

segments.name: Insta Help (professional/household help)
segments.commentary: Management said Insta Help is in a tougher base with Q2 revenue growth at 26.3% and the festive season falling in Q3; penetration in top 8 cities for largest categories is below 10%.

guidance_outlook: Consolidated breakeven target reiterated for Q3 FY28; management said it is confident, more than ever, of the ₹1,000 crore FY31 goal.
Management expects Q2 plus Q3 combined international growth in the range of 50% to 55%.
Fundraise of up to ₹2,500 crore is for flexibility, mainly for organic build-out of existing businesses and selective M&A; management said nothing imminent.
Native AC device launch: management expects one to two quarters of learning, limited largely to the app, and no material change to Native's trajectory.
Contribution margin target of 9–10% noted as the key lever; management said it is working towards it.
capex_capacity: Orders rose 63% QoQ to 6.23 million; 45% of new orders are reportedly from the Core Services' top categories, per management.
Management is onboarding professionals aggressively in the 3–4 months before the festive season to improve the liquidity coefficient.
Native's offline distribution is in a learning phase; M3 water purifier and Lock Ultra launched in modern retail with pull from offline ecosystem.
Gold premium service rollout: management said results are promising and it intends to scale it out across categories.
demand_pricing: Core Services average spend growth slowed to around 3% (vs historical 6–7%); management attributed this to mix change and season timing, and pass-through of densification benefits in pockets.
Instant service delivered in 30–60 minutes is offered in UAE and Singapore; management said no premium is currently charged.
Professional (partner) supply grew 16% YoY versus NTV growth of 26%; management declined to give forward partner-growth projections.
Hourly pricing roughly ₹200 and net order value roughly ₹300 for an average order of 1.5 hours; partner payout of ₹150 per utilised hour.
Management described the household-help TAM as range-bound with no single winner, and the AC TAM as roughly 10x water purifier TAM.

qa_highlights.question: What is driving Core Services' accelerating new-user acquisition and is it sustainable, with average spend growth slowing to 3%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited a stronger product with instant service in top 7–8 cities, AI-led training/QC improving word of mouth, densification, faster growth in Tier-2 markets and higher marketing. Average spend slowed due to mix, seasonality and some densification benefit passed to consumers.

qa_highlights.question: What is the use of proceeds from the ₹2,500 crore fundraise and the M&A framework?
qa_highlights.answer: Mainly for flexibility and organic build-out; M&A would be for consolidating existing categories or entering new categories, not new countries, with buy-vs-build tilting to buy if accretive. Nothing imminent.

qa_highlights.question: Why raise capital now given cash on balance sheet?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the raise is for flexibility, to be aggressive, pursue acquisitions and absorb downside in a high-competition scenario; not primarily to fund losses. Targets remain unchanged, and they would have changed short/medium-term targets if funding were insufficient.

qa_highlights.question: Does the Native AC launch and its allocation impact profitability timing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Native is on track for profitability, AC will be a disciplined build-up with R&D the bulk of losses, and any new category would take one to two quarters of learning before scale.

qa_highlights.question: Is professional supply or retention a rate limiter, and what is steady-state unit economics?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the challenge is retaining high-quality professionals, not sourcing. Experts care about net take-home pay; the company frames pricing and payouts as competitive. Steady-state unit economics remain under evaluation with a cited framework of payout ₹150 per hour, with ₹50 covering costs at best utilisation.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the acceleration in professional-services growth and what is the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said professional growth of 16% is a leading indicator; drivers are utilisation, targeting, and onboarding. Management declined to give specific projections.

qa_highlights.question: Will Native offline distribution expand pan-India in modern retail?
qa_highlights.answer: Offline share is small and in a learning phase; modern retail response is good; management will expand calibrated and slowly.

risks_watch: Competitive intensity in Core Services and International; management says losses are a deliberate choice.
Average spend growth slowing to 3% versus historical 6–7%.
Professional partner retention and churn as supply expands.
Native profitability and AC device adoption, with a one-to-two-quarter learning phase before scale.
Use and deployment of the ₹2,500 crore fundraise and any M&A execution.

544516|2026-03.headline: FY26 revenue rose 66% to Rs.319.6 Crores with PAT margin of 12.2%; FY27 guidance is Rs.500 Crores revenue at 12-13% PAT margin.
544516|2026-03.overview: FY26 revenue reached Rs.319.6 Crores (up 66% YoY), with H2 contributing Rs.229.1 Crores (up 114% YoY), and EBITDA of Rs.64.2 Crores at a 20.1% margin (EBITDA margin down from about 25% per analyst question). PAT was Rs.39.1 Crores (up 52%) at a 12.2% margin. Management said the Rs.1,000 Crores revenue milestone timeline may extend modestly because it declined to pursue low-margin re-tenders amid aluminium and stainless steel inflation. Management guided FY27 revenue of about Rs.500 Crores at 12-13% PAT margin, backed by an unexecuted order book of about Rs.469-487 Crores (figure varied in the call) and a Rs.1,200 Crores bid pipeline.

financial_highlights.change: +66% YoY vs Rs.192.4 Crores in FY25
+114% YoY vs Rs.107.3 Crores in H2 FY25
receivable days down 24 days; inventory days down 48 days

financial_highlights.metric: Net debt to equity at 31 Mar 2026

segments.name: Railways
segments.commentary: Largest growth driver; management says about 70% of the pipeline is railway, roughly Rs.900 Crores of the Rs.1,200 Crores bid pipeline, covering Atmanirbhar Bharat, Spark and Kavach coaches, Vande Bharat sleeper and Amrit Bharat turnkey contracts. Refurbishment is cited as a separate opportunity of about Rs.26,000 Crores sanctioned, with hoped-for orders of at least Rs.100 Crores this year.

segments.name: Metro
segments.commentary: About Rs.70 Crores of metro orders held, with another Rs.120 Crores expected within the Rs.1,200 Crores pipeline; Kolkata Metro turnkey contracts are named as a focus.

segments.name: Defence and aerospace
segments.commentary: Rs.29 Crores of current order book to execute this year, plus Rs.60-70 Crores expected from HAL tenders (mainly simulators, not AMCA airframe production). Proposed JV with Big Bang Boom Solutions to be incorporated before 15 June 2026; Airfloa committed about Rs.25 Crores, focused on autonomous drones and electronic warfare.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue target of approximately Rs.500 Crores with PAT margin of 12-13%; management said PAT would not fall below 12%.
Rs.1,000 Crores revenue milestone timeline may extend modestly; management also said it could be reached in FY28 or earlier if conditions allow.
Management said about 70-75% of the Rs.500 Crores FY27 target is covered by the existing order book, and 30-40% of the Rs.1,200 Crores pipeline is expected to execute in FY27.
R&D spend to rise to about 8-9% of sales this year from about 4% earlier; management later said R&D spend would be capitalised on the balance sheet.
Capex of Rs.30-40 Crores planned for FY27-28, including about Rs.30-35 Crores for a 14-acre facility with 50,000 to 1 lakh sq ft of initial shed space, expanding to 3-4 lakh sq ft.
Debt funding of about Rs.120 Crores at 8.25% from two banks: Rs.60 Crores sanctioned, the other Rs.60 Crores expected by end June 2026. No equity raise planned this year.
capex_capacity: Current capacity utilisation is about 90% of existing facility; two-shift operations in use since around December 2025.
New 14-acre facility planned: initial 50,000 to 1 lakh sq ft, later extending to 3-4 lakh sq ft; land already acquired and term loan discussions with bankers under way.

Machinery purchases, mostly from China, delayed because Chinese OEMs require an end-user certificate from the Government of India; management expected clarity in June 2026 and may switch to different machinery for lightweight rail interiors.
Plans to consolidate seven units into about two, reducing rent of roughly Rs.20-25 lakh per month.
Channel partner model in place to execute zonal railway contracts without building facilities in each region.
demand_pricing: Unexecuted order book about Rs.469-487 Crores (figure cited differently in different answers): Rs.415-420 Crores government and Rs.50-55 Crores non-government.
Bid pipeline about Rs.1,200 Crores with historical bid-win ratio of about 20-25%.

Raw material inflation: aluminium up more than 80% and stainless steel up 60-65% YoY; price variation clauses cover only about 50-60% of the increase, and accessories (30-35% of assembly cost) are not covered.
Competitors named: Kineco, Hindustan Fiberglass Works, DTL Ancillaries, Vibgyor, Universal Engineers; seating competitors Tata (with Fainsa), a Korean firm and firms from Mumbai and Bengaluru.

qa_highlights.question: How will working capital be funded and when will operating cash flow turn positive?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects about Rs.100-110 Crores of receivables collected by June end; receivable and working capital cycles targeted at 60-70 days from 90-95 days within 3-4 months. Debt of Rs.120 Crores is being raised.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the Rs.500 Crores FY27 target is covered by orders?
qa_highlights.answer: About 70-75% is covered by the existing order book, and 30-40% of the Rs.1,200 Crores pipeline is expected to execute in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Margin pressure and its causes in H2 FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: Aluminium and stainless steel inflation hit margins. Management said price variation covers only about 50-60% of losses, and it used advances, LCs and BGs to block vendor prices, limiting losses to 20-25% of the uncovered amount.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of added debt interest and R&D on the 12-13% PAT target?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said PAT would stay at or above 12%, citing higher-margin bids and that R&D spend would be deployed only when expected returns are met.

qa_highlights.question: Can FY28 revenue reach Rs.1,000 Crores and PAT Rs.150 Crores?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Rs.1,000 Crores could be reached even this year if all goes well and that FY28 could exceed Rs.1,000 Crores, without firm numbers.

qa_highlights.question: Does the Rs.500 Crores target hold given 90% utilisation and machinery delays?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said machinery delays would not affect FY27 turnover; two-shift operation and channel partners could add Rs.400-450 Crores from the Rs.320 Crores base.

risks_watch: Working capital: trade receivables of Rs.214 Crores at year-end; collection of about 70% expected by June, and cash conversion still negative.
Debt servicing: about Rs.120 Crores new debt at 8.25% adds interest cost of roughly Rs.10 Crores per year, per the analyst's calculation.
Raw material and commodity inflation, with price variation clauses covering only part of the increase.
Dependence on lumpy Indian Railways orders and back-loaded execution in H2.
Possible equity raise in FY28, which management did not rule out.
Defence revenue timing: management said defence products need 6-12 months of trials, and the Big Bang Boom JV is expected to be incorporated before 15 June 2026.
Inconsistent figures on order book (Rs.469 Crores vs Rs.486.9 Crores) and on EBITDA margin, which the analyst described as falling from 25% to 20%.
544516|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on FY27 execution and margins, but evasive on timing for the Rs.1,000 Crores milestone and on defence revenue, which management described as a long-cycle, first-time bid area. Several answers were repetitive or unclear, and management did not give firm numbers for the JV or the new facility.
key_quotes: Looking ahead, we are targeting a revenue of approximately Rs.500 Crores in FY 2027 while maintaining PAT margin in the range between 12% to 13%.
So I do not think that we can reduce our overall PAT level less than 12% for sure.
The bidding of Rs.1200 Crores is predominantly on the Indian railway sector.

rows.label: Volume growth

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.when: already announced; Rs.30-40 Crores over FY27-28
rows.why: The Rs.30-40 Crores capex for the new facility (Rs.30-35 Crores for the 14-acre site) is already planned and land is acquired, with Rs.120 Crores debt at 8.25% being raised to fund it and working capital.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management said Rs.1,000 Crores could be reached even this year if all goes well and FY28 could exceed it, but gave no firm numbers, and the Rs.1,000 Crores milestone timeline was itself said to be extending modestly.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Debt of about Rs.120 Crores at 8.25% adds roughly Rs.10 Crores of annual interest, receivables of Rs.214 Crores with cash conversion still negative, and machinery delays and raw material inflation could pressure the 12-13% PAT margin.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Management may switch machinery for lightweight rail interiors and the defence JV (autonomous drones and electronic warfare, Airfloa committed about Rs.25 Crores) is to be incorporated before 15 June 2026, but no product launch dates or revenue were given.

rows.label: Railway pipeline conversion (Rs.1,200 Cr bid pipeline, 20-25% win ratio)
rows.why: About Rs.900 Crores of the pipeline is railway and 30-40% is expected to execute in FY27, but the historical bid-win ratio is only 20-25%.

rows.label: Equity raise in FY28
rows.why: Management did not rule out an equity raise in FY28, though none is planned this year, and net debt to equity is 0.2 times after the Rs.120 Crores debt plan.

tone.note: Management was confident on FY27 execution (70-75% order cover) and the 12-13% PAT margin, but evasive on the Rs.1,000 Crores timeline and on defence revenue; analysts pressed on the EBITDA margin fall from about 25% to 20%, debt interest cost, and inconsistent order book figures.

544517|2026-03.headline: FY26 revenue rose 30% to INR 6,826 crore and EBITDA margin reached 3.35%; FY27 guided to about 20% revenue growth.
544517|2026-03.overview: Shankara Buildpro reported its first full year as a separately listed entity after the 1-1 demerger from Shankara Building Products, with FY26 revenue of INR 6,826 crore (+30% YoY) and Q4 revenue of INR 1,996 crore (+28% YoY, +20% QoQ). Steel volume crossed 1 million tonnes (10.16 lakh tonnes) and EBITDA rose 51% to INR 228 crore, with margin up 47 bps to 3.35%. PAT was INR 128 crore (+64%), with Q4 PAT of INR 42 crore (+42% YoY, +66% QoQ). Management flagged early-Q1 FY27 demand softness from the sharp price increases in March, tile supply disruption at Morbi, and a shortage of coated steel products, while guiding to about 20% growth in FY27.

financial_highlights.change: vs 3.05% in Q4 FY25 and 3.30% in Q3 FY26
+64% YoY; includes one-time INR 2.61 crore labour code provision

segments.name: Steel
segments.commentary: FY26 steel volume reached 10.16 lakh tonnes (+32% YoY) and Q4 volume was 2.89 lakh tonnes (+19% YoY, +11% QoQ). Steel tubes and pipes were about 6.9-7 lakh tonnes in FY26. Management puts steel EBITDA margin at about 3%.

segments.name: Non-steel
segments.commentary: FY26 non-steel revenue was INR 606 crore (+2% YoY) and Q4 was INR 161 crore. Non-steel EBITDA margin is about 6.5%, and non-steel is just under 10% of revenue. E-commerce revenue was INR 22 crore (+322% YoY).

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth of about 20% (management).
FY27 steel volume target of 1.2 million tonnes; FY28 target 1.4 million tonnes; 2 million tonnes by FY31. Steel volume growth of about 20% guided for FY27 and similar for FY28.
Steel tubes and pipes to rise from about 6.9-7 lakh tonnes in FY26 to 1 million tonnes in about three years (about 18-20% growth in FY27).
Non-steel revenue target INR 750 crore in FY27 (+25%) and INR 925 crore in FY28. Non-steel share to reach 15-20% over 4-5 years (later framed as 15-16% in 3-5 years).
EBITDA margin guided at about 3.3-3.5% for FY27; medium-term aspiration of about 4%, now expected by FY29 at the latest, with management saying it could be ASAP.

E-commerce revenue target INR 35 crore in FY27 and INR 50 crore in FY28. Fulfilment centres/stores: 7-10 in FY27 (3 already opened), then 4-5 per year from FY28. Capex INR 15-20 crore for FY27 expansion; FY27 rent about INR 10 crore.
capex_capacity: Plan to add 7-10 fulfilment centres/stores in FY27, with 3 already opened: Vasai (Maharashtra, steel tubes only), Thrissur (Kerala, steel) and Bengaluru (non-steel).
FY27 capex for the new fulfilment centres estimated at INR 15-20 crore.

Around 16 of the roughly 95-96 retail counters are leased from sister company Shankara Building Products; most fulfilment centres and warehouses are owned by it. Shankara Buildpro does not own any stores.

Expansion is planned within existing geographies for now; no move into new states is contemplated. Growth to date has come from southern territories and newer areas such as Gujarat and Madhya Pradesh.
demand_pricing: Sharp price increases in March 2026 across tiles, pipes and some steel are expected to weigh on April-June demand; some postponement of purchases is occurring. Management says normalisation is expected over the year.

Morbi tile output was badly hit from March due to gas shortages. Prices rose 10-15%, and supply is expected to normalise by June at higher prices. Coated steel products also faced shortages in March-May, now easing.

Management estimates Q1 FY27 volumes are about 10-15% above Q1 FY26, with about 50% of the quarter elapsed. It expects Q2 to be the stronger quarter, aided by monsoon-season recovery and festive demand.

Steel price volatility: hot-rolled coil fell in Q2-Q3 FY26 and rose sharply in Q4. Safeguard duties have firmed domestic prices. Inventory gain in Q4 was about INR 15 crore; Q1 gains are expected to largely square off as prices plateau in May-June.

Retail accounts for about 50% of steel sales. Roughly 50% of business comes from metros and about 50% from Tier-2 to rural areas. Top customers account for about 1% of revenue, so client concentration is low.

Management says it is pushing non-steel growth through CPVC/PVC (small base), UPVC roofing (imports from China under its Ganga brand), and recovery in CP, sanitaryware and tiles. Plastic pipe industry volumes fell in FY26, and Jal Jeevan disbursement was about one-third of budget.
Competition: larger players dump into metro dealer channels, but management says its decentralised retail model keeps it relatively shielded. Quick commerce is viewed as an opportunity, not a threat.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of March price hikes on demand and April/May trends?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says demand is hit to a small extent in April-June with some purchase postponement, but it expects the year to normalise.

qa_highlights.question: How will 1.2 million tonnes be achieved given Q1 slowdown?
qa_highlights.answer: Management corrected that the 1.2 million tonnes target covers all steel, not just tubes (about 7 lakh tonnes today). It expects Q1 to be slightly slow and Q2 to lead.

qa_highlights.question: What supports the 25% non-steel growth to INR 750 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Growth is expected from CPVC/PVC (small base), UPVC roofing with Chinese imports under the Ganga brand, and recovery in CP, sanitaryware and tiles.

qa_highlights.question: Why is margin improvement limited to 3.3-3.5% in FY27 despite operating leverage?
qa_highlights.answer: Management called the guidance conservative and said the aspiration is for the upper end of the range.

qa_highlights.question: What was the Q4 inventory gain and the one-off costs?
qa_highlights.answer: Q4 inventory gain was about INR 15 crore, offset by about INR 16 crore of one-offs: INR 2.5 crore demerger cost, INR 2.5 crore additional rent and INR 11 crore bad debt provision, all in other expenses.

qa_highlights.question: Where is the FY27 revenue growth and margin guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Revenue growth of about 20% in FY27; EBITDA margin of about 3.3-3.5%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the steel margin versus non-steel margin split?
qa_highlights.answer: Alex Varghese said non-steel EBITDA margin is about 6.5% and steel about 3%.

risks_watch: Q1 FY27 demand softness from price hikes; Q2 must carry the volume target. Monitor June recovery and Morbi tile supply normalisation.
Steel price volatility and inventory gains or losses; Q1 gains expected to square off.
Non-steel growth of 25% against a flat FY26 (+2%) and weak tile, plastic pipe and Jal Jeevan demand. Management's plan rests on new categories (CPVC/PVC, UPVC roofing).
Related-party dependence: most fulfilment centres and warehouses and about 16 of 95-96 counters are owned by sister company Shankara Building Products.
Competitive pressure from large new-age and corporate distributors, and the proposed IPO of a large OP business.

544517|2026-06.headline: Shankara Buildpro Q1 FY27 revenue rose 21% YoY to Rs 1,890 crore; steel volume grew 10% to 2.5 lakh tons and EBITDA margin was 3.26%.
544517|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations grew 21% YoY to Rs 1,890 crore and PAT rose 12% YoY to Rs 35.8 crore, led by steel volume growth and a recovery in non-steel. Management said April-May were weak due to West Asia-linked energy inflation and steel price volatility, with conditions improving through June and July. EBITDA was Rs 62 crore (3.26% margin), which management said included about Rs 10 crore of inventory erosion (roughly 50 bps) from a price correction in May-June. Management reiterated the 1.2 million-ton steel volume target, 20% steel and 25% non-steel volume growth, and a 3.5% steady-state EBITDA margin, and proposed a 1:5 stock split.

segments.name: Steel
segments.commentary: Volume of 2.5 lakh tons (+10% YoY) and revenue of Rs 1,725 crore (+21% YoY); pipes, tubes, flats and roofing all grew in volume. Management said the 1.2 million-ton FY27 target is intact.

segments.name: Non-steel
segments.commentary: Revenue of Rs 165 crore (+15% YoY). Fittings and sanitary ware, the largest category, grew 32%; accessories and electricals grew about 40% on a smaller base; tiles were hit hardest in April.

Steady-state EBITDA margin target of 3.5%+; management said about 3.8% would have been reached without the Rs 10 crore inventory erosion.
Medium term (FY28 onward): EBITDA margin of around 4%, while maintaining 20% steel and 25% non-steel volume growth.
Target of 2 million tons in around 4 years; the 20% growth path is the baseline, with new territories and stores as upside.
About 5 more fulfilment centres or stores planned in the coming quarters, taking FY27 additions to roughly 8-9 (3 added in Q1).
Proposed 1:5 stock split (face value Rs 10 to Rs 2), pending shareholder and regulatory approvals; total paid-up capital unchanged.
capex_capacity: Three fulfilment centres/stores added in Q1 FY27 (Mangalore, Mumbai, Thrissur), plus 34 customer touchpoints across 45 towns and cities in 10 states.
About 5 more fulfilment centres planned in the coming quarters.
Planned investment in value-added steel infrastructure (cut-to-length, laser cutting) and warehousing.
Cash use priorities: private-label products (with promotion spend), value-added steel investment, and reducing acceptance-based borrowing. Acquisitions are 'on the table' but none named.
demand_pricing: Steel prices spiked in March-April, then corrected sharply in May-June, causing inventory erosion of about Rs 10 crore; prices have stabilised over July and early August.
Management said the Q4 FY26 inventory gain was about Rs 15 crore.
Volume recovered in June (about 1 lakh MT of rebound cited) and management said the momentum continued into July.
Non-steel tile demand was near zero in April (Morbi gas/energy shock) and recovered in May-June; PVC/UPVC roofing uptake is good.
Competitive intensity from well-funded enterprise-focused players has eased in the last couple of quarters; management is de-prioritising TMT and focusing on flats.
Retail accounts for about 50-55% of total volume. Ticket sizes range from Rs 500 to Rs 1.5 crore across 25 verticals, 75 categories and over 100 brands, with over 2 lakh SKUs.

qa_highlights.question: Can 22-23% volume growth be achieved for the rest of FY27 to reach 1.2 MT, given the high H2 base?
qa_highlights.answer: Sukumar Srinivas said June volume growth was very positive and July continued the trend, and he is confident of 1.2 MT barring unforeseen headwinds.

qa_highlights.question: What were the margin impacts from fixed-price contracts and inventory, and what is the steady-state margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Contracts carried over from March into April forced supply at high prices, and the May-June price drop eroded about Rs 10 crore (about 50 bps). Ex this, margin would have been about 3.8%; steady state 3.5%+ is the target.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the company guiding for 25% non-steel growth when peers are not showing similar optimism?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited 32% growth in CP and sanitary ware, a tile recovery from May-June, and PVC/UPVC roofing traction; the CP/sanitary segment is expected to drive most of the growth.

qa_highlights.question: What explains the interest cost, given about Rs 75 crore of debt?
qa_highlights.answer: Alex Varghese said about Rs 500 crore of acceptances (LCs opened and discounted, with the company bearing interest) bring total borrowings to about Rs 575 crore; the interest cost mainly comes from acceptances.

qa_highlights.question: Is 20% revenue growth achievable at a 3.5% EBITDA margin, and is there margin expansion in FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Dhananjay Mirlay Srinivas said the company is on track for 20% volume growth at 3.5% margin, and medium-term aims for about 4% EBITDA margin with 20% steel and 25% non-steel volume growth.

qa_highlights.question: How long to reach 2 MT, and what new categories are planned?
qa_highlights.answer: Target is about 4 years to 2 MT via new territories, stores and market share gains; new steel infrastructure for cut-to-length and value-added products, and expanding white-label private labels in retail.

qa_highlights.question: What is the volume/price split of the 21% revenue growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Sukumar Srinivas said price played little part; steel prices were high and then softened, so the effect was largely neutral. He said a detailed split would be shared offline.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the company guiding for a 3.5% margin when adjusted Q1 margin is about 3.8%?
qa_highlights.answer: Sukumar Srinivas said management is taking a cautious path because steel inventory gains and losses are outside its control, and it prefers to be prudent.

qa_highlights.question: What is the steel business profitability and outlook for flats?
qa_highlights.answer: Non-steel has an 8-10% EBITDA margin, so steel is trending above 3% overall; diversifying into flats and multiple steel products should help grow EBITDA.

544521|2026-03.headline: VMS TMT Q4 FY26 revenue INR241 crore, net profit INR2.29 crore; FY26 revenue INR840 crore and PAT INR21 crore.
544521|2026-03.overview: Management reported Q4 FY26 total revenue of INR241 crore, EBITDA of INR11.94 crore and net profit of INR2.29 crore, with FY26 revenue of INR840 crore, EBITDA of INR62.31 crore and net profit of INR21 crore. Management credited the CCM/hot-charging billet integration for lower raw material cost and about INR1,000-1,500 per ton of margin improvement. Borrowings were repaid during the year, and a 15 MW captive solar project is being commissioned in tranches. Management said no capacity expansion is currently planned, and utilisation is about 70-75% for both billets and TMT.

segments.commentary: Core and only product line; sold under Kamdhenu brand in Gujarat at about INR1,500/ton premium over regional brands. Gujarat market about 4.5-5 lakh tons a year; company sells about 15,000 tons per month.

segments.name: Billets (integrated)
segments.commentary: Company now makes its own billets from scrap via CCM and hot charging; stopped buying billets externally. Scrap bought at about INR35,000/ton versus INR42,000/ton earlier billet purchase price. Utilisation about 70-75%.

Management says it will fund any future expansion from internal accruals over the next 2-3 years.

TMT capacity utilisation about 70-75% of installed capacity; billet utilisation about 70-75%.

Solar payback stated at five years.

qa_highlights.question: What tangible benefits from the billet facility on raw material cost and margins?

544521|2026-06.headline: VMS TMT Q1 FY27 total income rose 16.16% YoY to ₹247.88 crore, but EBITDA fell about 41% and PAT dropped to ₹2.45 crore on imported scrap costs.
544521|2026-06.overview: Total income for Q1 FY27 was ₹247.88 crore versus ₹213.39 crore a year earlier, up 16.16% YoY, with TMT sales volume and average realisation both stated as higher. Management attributed the margin squeeze to a sharp rise in imported scrap prices linked to the Iran conflict, plus a rupee depreciation effect on cargo bought earlier at lower dollar rates; PAT fell to ₹2.45 crore and EBITDA declined about 41% per the analyst's figures. Billet capacity commissioning and the 15 MW captive solar plant (12 MW live from 7 August) were highlighted as cost levers. Management guided margin recovery from Q3 FY27, with the proposed Aditya Ultra Steel amalgamation presented as a further scale driver.

Q4 gross sales were about INR 750 crore (+12% YoY), with Q4 gross margin of about 12.5% of gross sales, helped by year-end rebates and OEM pressure. Working capital improved to 30 net working capital days, and operating cash flow of INR 108 crore exceeded PAT for the first time. Management reiterated FY27 growth above FY26 and flagged possible dividend or buyback if no inorganic deal is done.

544523|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 gross sales rose 5.7% to INR 641.2 crore while PAT jumped 51.7% to INR 15.7 crore on margin recovery.
544523|2026-06.overview: Gross sales were INR 641.2 crore (up 5.7% YoY) and gross margin widened to 8.1% of gross sales from 6.8%, lifting gross margin INR 52 crore (up 26.5%). Operating EBITDA was INR 20.2 crore (up 27.7%) and PAT INR 15.7 crore (up 51.7%), helped by lower finance costs. Cybersecurity grew 8% and DCI grew about 180%, while ILM fell about 60% as customer budgets shifted toward GPU and data-centre spend. Management reiterated 20% growth in gross sales and PAT for FY27 and said H2 is seasonally stronger. The CEO is stepping down, with the Chairman/MD and Executive Director jointly overseeing the role.

qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed ILM's fall to budgets reallocated to GPU and data-centre spend and expects ILM to return from Q3. It said cybersecurity is growing and is expected to be 45-50% of sales annualised.

qa_highlights.question: Why were Q1 gross sales soft and why has gross profit growth lagged guidance for several quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the FY26 base had a large GSTN deal of about INR 150 crore billed in Q2 and that large deals cluster in H2. It said the Q1 FY26 margin was depressed by rupee depreciation and low-margin deals, so a 10% gross profit growth in FY26 is not the steady-state rate.

qa_highlights.question: Does the 46% annuity share mean net new sales are weak?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said annuity was 43.1% in Q1 FY26 and that the roughly 3-point rise came from upsell and price increases at existing customers, not a hit to net new business.

qa_highlights.question: How does the company benefit from data-centre build-outs such as Reliance-Meta?
qa_highlights.answer: Krishna Raj Sharma said public data centres mostly contract directly with OEMs, so the larger opportunity is private/captive data centres. Sunil Pillai said the TAM will be sized once capacity is online.

qa_highlights.question: Will the CEO be replaced and is inorganic growth planned?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the CEO is leaving for personal reasons and that the Chairman/MD and Executive Director will jointly oversee the role, with new CBO, CRO and CTO appointed. Inorganic growth is being explored, with no material progress announced.

544525|2026-09.headline: GK Energy H1 FY27 revenue rose 38.9% to INR 907.8 crore, with Q2 revenue up 12.3% to INR 402.7 crore and receivables still stretched at 204 days.

Q2, seasonally the weakest quarter, saw revenue up 12.3% to INR 402.7 crore, EBITDA of INR 74.4 crore (18.5% margin) and PAT of INR 49.4 crore. Management highlighted INR 377.5 crore of customer collections since 30 September, which cut receivable days from 204 to about 128 on its calculation. The company is widening from solar pumps into rooftop solar and its first utility-scale BESS order (150 MW / 300 MWh).

segments.commentary: Management says retail rooftop is growing strongly; more than 2,000 systems installed and 4,000-5,000 system demand cited. Institutional order to install one lakh rooftop systems; an order of around INR 450 crore was referenced on the call.

segments.name: BESS (battery storage, utility-scale)
segments.commentary: First order for 150 MW / 300 MWh utility-scale installation. Company plans to build its own BESS plants and sell power to DISCOMs under a fixed-revenue model for 15 years; intends to expand to 2 GW in the midterm.

qa_highlights.question: How can FY27 margins hold at 17-18% given Q1 about 16% and Q2 about 17%?

qa_highlights.question: What drives 35-40% growth if PM KUSUM is delayed, and how does it square with the INR 788 crore order book?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to the existing pump orders, retail rooftop, and Magel Tyala 7 pipeline; it said about INR 500 crore of new orders must be secured to reach INR 2,200 crore total.

qa_highlights.question: Why are pump receivables so stretched at over six months, and is the model perennially long-dated?

544526|2026-03.headline: FY26 revenue rose about 111% to INR 45,484 million, but Q4 EBITDA margin compressed sharply on input-cost inflation and rupee depreciation.
544526|2026-03.overview: Saatvik reported record FY26 revenue of INR 45,484 million (up about 111% YoY), EBITDA of INR 5,811 million (12.78% margin) and PAT of INR 3,571 million (7.85% margin). Q4 revenue hit a record INR 16,077 million, but EBITDA fell to INR 1,166 million and PAT to INR 604 million, as silver, aluminium, copper and oil-linked input costs rose and the rupee weakened after the war that began 20 February 2026. Management said fixed-price contracts could not pass on these increases immediately. Cell capacity expansion is the main near-term story: 2.4 GW cell line is targeted to start production in H2 FY27, and the cell plan is now 6 GW.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the Q4 EBITDA decline, and what margins do new orders carry?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited higher silver, aluminium, copper and oil-linked costs, rupee depreciation, and fixed-price contracts signed before the war that could not be repriced immediately. Some new orders can pass costs through and others must absorb them, depending on the customer.

qa_highlights.question: When will the 2.4 GW and 6 GW cell lines start and stabilise?
qa_highlights.answer: Module equipment move-in starts June 2026 and cell equipment move-in July 2026, with production starting in H2 FY27. Phase II (3.6 GW) civil work starts August 2026; full 6 GW by June-July 2027.

qa_highlights.question: What are the FY27-FY28 capex and debt plans?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 expansion capex is about INR 1,700 crore, funded by debt and accrual-funded equity. FY28 capex is about INR 1,800-2,000 crore for ingot. Debt-equity is expected to stay between 1.0 and 1.5 times, currently 0.65.

qa_highlights.question: Why has cash conversion been low, and why did creditor days fall?
qa_highlights.answer: Large PSU orders carry 90-120 day recovery cycles, with Q4 dispatches recovering in April-May. Creditor days normalised as the company paid suppliers faster to secure better pricing during the volatility.

qa_highlights.question: Will cells be sold externally, and what are the EPC and order-execution details?
qa_highlights.answer: The 6 GW cell capacity is currently for captive use, but management will decide on external sales based on margins. Execution timeline is about 18 months, EPC contribution is about 3-4% and stays in that range in FY27.

544526|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 revenue fell to INR 5,110 mn (from INR 9,157 mn YoY) on 334 MW sales; EBITDA margin rose to 8.33% while confirmed order book stands at ~6.35 GW.
544526|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 was a weak quarter: sales of 334 MW were down from 579 MW a year earlier and 1,050 MW in Q4 FY26, as customers deferred procurement and management chose to execute only margin-accretive orders. Revenue fell to INR 5,110 mn and PAT to INR 54 mn. Management said the EBITDA margin of 8.33% was better than the 7.25% in Q4 FY26. The Odisha cell line (2.4 GW) is near ramp-up with ALMM-2 inspection planned for September 2026, and management is pinning margin recovery on cell volumes in H2 FY27. Management kept FY27 guidance unchanged, but the call contained no numbers for Q2.

segments.commentary: Operational module capacity is 4.8 GW. Q1 sales were 334 MW against production of 408 MW. Management said the module market has become crowded.

segments.commentary: Non-module revenue was 4-5% of total, with a target of 7-8% in FY27 and 15% next year. Melcon was acquired mid-Q1 and the transformer market is about INR 30,000 crore, targeted at INR 1,000-1,500 crore revenue in 3-4 years.

guidance_outlook: FY27 guidance unchanged: 3.5-4 GW sales, revenue of about INR 6,000 crore, EBITDA margin of about 12%, PAT margin of 6-7%.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the sharp YoY EBITDA margin compression despite a strong order book?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited a crowded module market, higher commodity, freight and forex costs from the geopolitical situation, and weak customer demand. It also said it declined to execute orders where input costs could not be passed on. Q1 margin of 8.33% was better than Q4 FY26's 7.25%.

qa_highlights.question: When does cell manufacturing start and what utilisation is expected?
qa_highlights.answer: Ramp-up is expected by end-August or early September 2026, with 200 MW per month from the 2.4 GW line. Management expects about 80% utilisation by Q4 FY27. Full ramp-up is expected in about three months.

qa_highlights.question: Debt peak and capex needs for FY27-28?
qa_highlights.answer: Debt is about INR 1,250 crore. Capex incurred is about INR 1,000 crore out of a roughly INR 3,500 crore programme. Net debt is expected to peak at INR 2,200-2,400 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Why did demand slow in Q1 when the ALMM transition was expected to pull volumes forward?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said developers waited because input costs rose after the Iran war began on 20 February, and force majeure notices and expected DCR extensions pushed projects out. Two tariff regimes (before and after 30 June) also encouraged waiting, which left demand subdued in May and June.

qa_highlights.question: Could you give the FY28 outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give FY28 numbers until Q3 FY27. It said large utility projects tendered from December 2025 (18-24 month cycles) will drive DCR demand from April 2027, making FY28 a milestone year.

qa_highlights.question: What is the non-module business plan and transformer opportunity?
qa_highlights.answer: Non-module business is 4-5% of revenue, targeted at 7-8% in FY27 and 15% next year. Melcon was acquired mid-Q1. Management targets 8-10% of a transformer market of about INR 30,000 crore (INR 55,000 crore by 2031) and INR 1,000-1,500 crore revenue in 3-4 years.

rows.why: Q1 sales fell 42% YoY to 334 MW (vs 579 MW) and 68% QoQ from 1,050 MW; FY27 guide of 3.5-4 GW needs roughly 3.2-3.7 GW in Q2-Q4 (about 1.1-1.2 GW/quarter), versus a 334 MW Q1 base, and no Q2 number was given, while the 6.35 GW order book and cell ramp support recovery.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.when: Phase 2 site work by end-Q2 FY27; encapsulant equipment anno
rows.why: Phase 2 (3.6 GW cell, INR 1,600-1,700 crore) is already approved with site work starting by end-Q2 FY27, Phase 3 (6 GW ingot/wafer) planning has started, and the encapsulant capacity expansion from 2 GW to 5 GW is due to be announced next quarter.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY27 guidance was held unchanged despite Q1 sales of 334 MW and revenue of INR 5,110 mn, and management gave no Q2 numbers, so a raise is not signalled.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Q1 revenue fell to INR 5,110 mn vs INR 16,077 mn in Q4 FY26, FY27 guidance of ~INR 6,000 crore implies roughly INR 8,900 mn/quarter over Q2-Q4, and any cell ramp or ALMM-2 slip (to 1 January 2027) would push the 12% EBITDA margin case back.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: DCR cell sales for own use have started with DCR cell margins quoted at 18-20%, and the non-module business (Melcon acquired mid-Q1) is targeted to rise from 4-5% to 7-8% of revenue in FY27 and 15% next year.

rows.label: 6.35 GW confirmed order book executing over 12-18 months
rows.why: Order book of about 6.35 GW (132% of 4.8 GW module capacity), valued at about INR 8,200 crore, with fresh orders of INR 138 crore (execution by Dec 2026) and about INR 400 crore (execution by Mar 2027) support near-term volumes.

rows.label: ALMM-2 inspection and postponed effective date
rows.why: ALMM-2 was postponed from 1 July 2026 to 1 January 2027 due to domestic cell shortages, and the inspection is planned for September 2026, which gates DCR cell demand and the cell-led margin thesis.

rows.label: Net debt peak of INR 2,200-2,400 crore
rows.why: Total debt is about INR 1,250 crore with debt-to-equity at 0.99x and about INR 1,000 crore of the roughly INR 3,500 crore capex programme spent, so net debt is set to rise before any deleveraging.

tone.note: Management was confident on the Odisha cell ramp and the integration story but cautious on near-term numbers: no Q2 figures, FY28 deferred to Q3 FY27, and the high-double-digit cell EBITDA uplift left unquantified; analysts pushed on the sharp YoY margin compression and volume decline.

544527|2026-03.headline: Atlanta Electricals Q4 FY26 revenue rose 81.7% YoY to INR747.6 crore with EBITDA margin near 20%; FY26 term debt fully repaid.
544527|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue from operations was INR747.6 crore (+81.7% YoY, +58.5% QoQ), with EBITDA of INR149.6 crore (19.99% margin vs 16.7% a year earlier) and PAT of INR102.2 crore (+128.9% YoY). Consolidated FY26 revenue was INR1,851.5 crore (+48.8%), EBITDA INR344.4 crore (18.6% margin, +300 bps) and PAT INR201.8 crore (+70.1%). All term loans were repaid by 31 March 2026, and the Vadod unit 4 received PGCIL approval for up to 400 kV on 2 April 2026. Management flagged a planned inventory drawdown ahead of April maintenance shutdowns and a mineral oil shortage in Q4 linked to the West Asia conflict.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said margins on 220 kV and below are stable; the gain came from 220 kV scale-up. Margins expected to stay stable going forward.

qa_highlights.answer: Per-MVA pricing is linked to commodity prices (steel, copper, oil) via customer contracts, so it rises with commodities; it will fall as 500 MVA class 400/765 kV units come in.

qa_highlights.answer: No data centre order in the book; management is in talks with customers. HVDC not targeted until 400/765 kV prototypes are validated.

qa_highlights.answer: About 75% of the INR2,493 crore order book has price variation; no commodity hit in Q4, and no hit is expected in Q1 as far as management can see.

qa_highlights.answer: Backward integration is for supply chain control and quality, not margin; margins expected to remain fairly stable after 400/765 kV development costs.

qa_highlights.answer: 220 kV and below takes 12-18 months; 80-85% of the current order book executes in FY27. Small 400 kV portion delivers from December to March.

544527|2026-06.headline: Atlanta Electricals Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 48% YoY to INR466.33 crore; record order inflow of INR972.42 crore lifted order book to INR3,116.63 crore.
544527|2026-06.overview: Revenue grew 48% YoY to INR466.33 crore, driven mainly by volume from newly commissioned plants, with management saying pricing and product mix were broadly unchanged. Gross margin rose 130 bps to 27.3% and EBITDA margin expanded to 16.5% from 15.5% a year ago, though both moderated from Q4 FY26 seasonally. Order inflow was a record INR972.42 crore, taking the unexecuted order book to about INR3,117 crore, of which about INR2,400 crore is expected to execute in FY27. Management reiterated a 40% revenue CAGR target and a 17-18% margin range, while 400 kV and 765 kV product timelines were pushed out and largely remain conditional.

segments.name: Product mix by voltage class
segments.commentary: 220 kV class was 56% of Q1 revenue, 66 kV class 25%, and 132 kV class about 5.5%. Power transformers were about 79% of revenue, with auto, inverter duty and other products making up the balance.

segments.name: End market
segments.commentary: Transmission and distribution contributed about 66% of revenue and renewable energy about 19%, with thermal power and other industrial making up the rest.

segments.name: Order book by voltage
segments.commentary: 220 kV and above transformers are over 55% of the order book; 400 kV transformers and reactors account for nearly INR275 crore. Management said the entire record Q1 inflow is 220 kV and below.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue target of 40% YoY growth, applied to FY26 revenue of INR1,851 crore (per CFO); management also cited a 40% CAGR for three years.
EBITDA margin expected around 17-18% for the year, with raw material inflation expected to persist but margins sustainable at the Q1 level.
About INR2,400 crore of the ~INR3,100 crore unexecuted order book is due for execution in FY27.
Inverter duty transformer facility (~5,000 MVA) targeted for commissioning by end-December 2026.
Export target of about 15% of revenue within three years; no export revenue in Q1 FY27 and first export execution expected in FY28.
Management expects meaningful revenue from 400 kV transformers from FY28, with 765 kV tech tie-up targeted by end-Q2 FY27 and first 765 kV product by Q4 FY27.
capex_capacity: Installed manufacturing capacity of 63,060 MVA; Q1 sales-based utilisation of 4,381 MVA, of which Vadod produced 1,520 MVA and Ankhi (Jambusar) 320 MVA.
Inverter duty transformer facility adds ~5,000 MVA; construction on track for commissioning by end-December 2026.
Vadod Unit 4 received Power Grid approval for 400 kV class manufacturing; first 400 kV unit under engineering completion, with short-circuit test planned around quarter-end (Q1 FY27 end or early Q2).
Tank and radiator backward-integration facility adjacent to Vadod: INR15-20 crore spent so far against about INR180 crore planned; tanks and radiators are 4-5% of transformer cost.
765 kV plan: first product to be made at Ankhi once technical tie-up closes; Power Grid revalidation needed in new name. Short-circuit test requirement for 765 kV not yet finalised.
demand_pricing: Record order inflow of INR972.42 crore in Q1 FY27; order book INR3,116.63 crore as of 30 June 2026.
Key orders: INR291.68 crore from RVPNL (160 MVA, 50 MVA, 31.5 MVA power transformers) and INR285.15 crore from PSTCL (23 units of 160 MVA 220/66 kV transformers).
Pricing passed through via price variation clauses in purchase orders; per-MVA realisation described as unchanged across kV classes, with raw material inflation passed on.
Management saw no pricing or bidding-intensity impact from Chinese manufacturers being allowed into PSU tenders; none had participated yet.
No data-centre orders in current order book. Management expects order booking to peak in Q2 and mid-Q3 FY27.
Management said CRGO steel prices and supply are not under pressure in the short term; DGTR anti-dumping verdict expected by end-March 2027.

qa_highlights.question: Will the new 400 kV capacity pressure incremental margins or order inflow?
qa_highlights.answer: Niral Patel said Q1 was the highest order inflow in at least 2-2.5 years, with no visible pricing correction in the market.

qa_highlights.question: Are inventory builds speculative ahead of raw material volatility?
qa_highlights.answer: Anand Sharma said procurement is strictly job-to-job with no speculation on commodity prices; inventory build is for the next quarter's executions.

qa_highlights.question: What are the 765 kV tech tie-up terms?
qa_highlights.answer: Niral Patel said the deal combines a one-time fee of USD3-5 million and royalty of 2-4% for at least three to four years, on 765 kV products only; the partner is not named.

qa_highlights.question: Can margins be sustained at 17-18%?
qa_highlights.answer: Mehul Mehta said FY25 and FY26 margins ended at 15.56% and 18.52%, and that 17-18% is the expected range, with raw material price increases continuing.

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin differential for 400 kV and 765 kV?
qa_highlights.answer: Anand Sharma said these products should earn better margins than 220 kV or 132 kV, but the exact differential will only be known after first prototypes and commercial production.

qa_highlights.question: How much FY27 revenue is implied?
qa_highlights.answer: Mehul Mehta said a 40% YoY increase on FY26 revenue of INR1,851 crore is the guidance.

risks_watch: Execution timing on 400 kV: short-circuit test for the first 400 kV unit slipped from June-July to around quarter-end; balance order quantity depends on passing it.
765 kV entry depends on closing the technical tie-up (targeted Q2 FY27), government approvals on the partner side, Power Grid revalidation and an unresolved short-circuit test requirement.

Capacity additions by peers (including mention of CG Power and Transformer Rectifiers, about 60,000 MVA in the next 3-4 months per an analyst) could pressure pricing; management expects margin protection through 400/765 kV and exports.
Raw material cost pressure from geopolitics and CRGO steel anti-dumping investigation; Q1 gross margin fell QoQ.
Working capital: inventory days at 105 and inventory build in Q1; monitor cash conversion cycle (~83 days).
Export revenue is zero so far; the 15% export target is three years out.

544529|2026-09.headline: Aptus Pharma H1 FY27 revenue rose to Rs 48.90 crore from Rs 14.38 crore, with PAT of about Rs 5.08 crore; no forward guidance given.
544529|2026-09.overview: Management reported H1 FY27 (half-year ended 30 September 2026) revenue from operations of about Rs 48.90 crore versus Rs 14.38 crore a year earlier, with EBITDA of about Rs 7.68 crore, PBT of about Rs 6.83 crore and PAT of about Rs 5.08 crore. The strategy was reiterated as three pillars: manufacturing (about 20% of portfolio self-made by March 2028), pan-India expansion (46% geographic coverage by March 2027, pan-India by 2029) and international expansion. Management declined to give any quantitative guidance on revenue, EBITDA, PAT or capex returns during the Q&A.

544530|2026-03.headline: Anand Rathi Q4 FY26 consolidated PAT rose 125.7% YoY to ₹416 million on revenue of ₹2,557 million, while the MTF book fell 10.53% QoQ.

segments.name: Non-broking (MTF, distribution, other)
segments.commentary: MTF book ₹11,019 million with zero NPA and ~61% of exposure from clients with balances below ₹1 crore. Distribution income rose 44.1% in FY26 to ₹1,129 million, spanning MF, PMS, AIF, insurance, bonds, structured products and FDs.

segments.name: Asset management / custody
segments.commentary: AUM ₹77,876 million (+21% YoY); assets under custody ₹944,155 million (+16% YoY). Insurance corporate agency licence obtained in FY26; life and health insurance distribution has started.

guidance_outlook: Target revenue mix of 50:50 between broking and non-broking, with both growing steadily; management said it is not yet happy with the current 51:49 split and expects to reach 50:50 over time.
Management expects non-broking to grow about 40-45% annually for the first few years, and broking about 15% a year.
Overall revenue growth aim of about 15-20% YoY.
Earlier guidance of an MTF book of ₹15,000 million by FY26 was missed; the book ended at ₹11,019 million.
Debt-equity ceiling set at a maximum of 1.5x; current ratio is about 0.6x.
capex_capacity: MTF book contracted 10.53% QoQ in Q4 FY26 after RBI policy changes narrowed bank and NBFC funding avenues for capital market intermediaries; management said the company had to control growth and preserve cash for margin requirements.

IPO completed in September 2025 raising ₹745 crore, used mainly for working capital.

qa_highlights.answer: Two dormant depository clients lost securities through fraudulent off-market transfers noticed about a year later. Recoveries will be booked only when reasonably certain.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said distribution is seasonal, with insurance sales concentrated in January–March; the April–June fall was driven by insurance, while other products grew. Trail revenue was also hit by the March market fall.

qa_highlights.answer: MTF yield is about 14%. Management said spreads depend on liquidity, with borrowing costs currently higher, and that higher costs can be passed to clients.

rows.label: Distribution trail income catching up

544531|2026-03.headline: True Colors FY26 revenue rose 29.22% to INR 301.55 crore, with EBITDA margin at 15.58% and PAT at INR 31.16 crore, but operating cash flow was negative.
544531|2026-03.overview: FY26 revenue from operations was INR 301.55 crore (up 29.22% YoY), EBITDA INR 46.98 crore (15.58% margin) and PAT INR 31.16 crore (10.33% margin). Recurring revenue from ink, sublimation paper and spares was about 50.25% of revenue. Operating cash flow was negative (about INR 35 crore), which management attributed to MSME payment-term compliance, Konica Minolta advance-payment terms and a rise in receivables to INR 111 crore at March-end, now reported at about INR 93 crore. Management is moving ink from trading to in-house manufacturing under the INKIA brand, with a phased capex plan.

financial_highlights.change: Prior-year H2 margin cited as 17.5%; full-year FY25 margin cited as about 18%
Compared with a figure of about INR 31 crore in the analyst's question (sign and comparison not clarified)

financial_highlights.change: Nearly doubled YoY per analyst; about INR 93 crore as of the call date
